metadata.title: UK rents forecast to rise twice as fast as house prices over the next 3 years
metadata.contentSnippet: Hamptons forecasts UK rents will rise 14.2% by 2029, twice as fast as house prices, while Lloyds finds buying cheaper than renting in seven cities.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: UK rents forecast to rise twice as fast as house prices over the next 3 years
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Rents are expected to rise around twice as fast as house prices. Newly-let properties are forecast to see this surge over the next three years, according to Hamptons. The property company predicts that across Britain, private rents for newly-let homes will increase by 14.2% between the fourth quarter of 2026 and the fourth quarter of 2029. In comparison, house prices are expected to grow by a more modest 7.2% over the same period. Hamptons attributes the rising rents to a limited supply of rental properties and ongoing affordability challenges for first-time buyers. Aneisha Beveridge, head of research at Hamptons, said: "With fewer homes entering the rental market, competition between tenants is likely to keep rents rising faster than house prices over the next few years. "For landlords, that creates a delicate balancing act because higher costs do not automatically translate into higher rents. "Historically, landlords have had limited scope to pass those costs on, with rents set by wider market conditions rather than their individual bills. "But as costs have risen across the sector and rental supply has fallen, the bar has shifted, allowing more of those increases to feed through into higher rents. "There is, however, a silver lining for investors. "With rents rising faster than house prices, yields are improving, particularly across parts of southern England. "In London, that has already started to tempt some landlords back into the market. "For tenants, though, a smaller rental market means more competition and continued pressure on affordability. "Existing tenants may initially be more insulated from rising rents, but the new-let and existing-tenancy markets do not operate independently. "Over time, stronger new-let rental growth is likely to filter through to the wider market." Hamptons expects rents on all privately rented homes—not just newly-let properties—to rise by 10.9% over the next three years. The firm said rent growth on newly-agreed lets could begin to slow in 2028 and 2029 as mortgage rates are expected to decline. However, many long-term challenges in the rental sector are likely to persist. In a separate report, Lloyds analysed the cost of buying versus renting in 12 major UK cities and found that owning a home could be cheaper than renting in seven of them. The analysis was based on Office for National Statistics (ONS) data and assumed a 5% deposit. Lloyds' research indicated that in Glasgow, buyers could save £288 per month compared to renters. In Newcastle, the monthly saving was estimated at £187, while in Bristol, buyers could save £139 per month. Andrew Asaam, mortgages director at Lloyds, said: "Higher mortgage rates have seen the cost of borrowing increase this year, making that affordability calculation even more important. "But in many cities across the UK, buyers could still pay less for their mortgage than they would typically be charged in rent – giving them an immediate saving as well as a place of their own." Meanwhile, property consultancy Knight Frank has revised its UK house price forecasts downward. It now expects house price growth of just 1% in 2027, down from the 3% forecasted in April. Knight Frank said that cumulative UK house price growth over the five years to 2031 is now expected to reach 14.2%, compared to its previous estimate of 20.4%. The downgrade reflects concerns about the political climate, higher borrowing costs, and ongoing geopolitical instability, all of which are expected to dampen buyer demand and market confidence.

metadata.title: Post Office warns Christmas shoppers to post early ahead of busiest parcel day
metadata.contentSnippet: Post Office expects December 7 to be its busiest Christmas parcel day, with more than 100m items expected.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Post Office warns Christmas shoppers to post early ahead of busiest parcel day
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Monday, December 7, is expected to be the Post Office’s busiest day for sending festive parcels. With customers across the UK preparing to post gifts to loved ones both domestically and overseas, the Post Office anticipates handling more than 100 million parcels during the two-month Christmas period. Shanaz Nandha, postmaster at Biggleswade Post Office, said: "Christmas is always a busy time for us in branch, with lots of customers sending presents to friends and family across the UK and overseas." The Post Office is encouraging people to post early wherever possible, especially for international deliveries. While Monday December 7 is forecast to be peak posting day, the Post Office said it is reminding customers they do not need to wait until the busiest period. Popular overseas destinations for Christmas parcels include the United States, Australia, Ireland, Germany and Poland. The Post Office suggested that people check last posting dates, particularly if they are sending items overseas. Royal Mail has also published its recommended last posting dates for UK services: December 19 is also the last posting date for Royal Mail Tracked Returns 48 to reach the sender before Christmas. The Post Office advises customers to check their branch's final acceptance time, which varies between branches. Royal Mail says its published dates are subject to change and advises customers to post as early as possible. It also recommends sending international items early, with published delivery aims available in its country guides.

metadata.title: Further details emerge after armed police descend on Cambridgeshire village
metadata.contentSnippet: Two boys have been arrested after armed police descended on the Brookland Centre in Sutton, near Ely.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Further details emerge after armed police descend on Cambridgeshire village
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: The reason why armed police descended on a quiet Cambridgeshire village has been revealed. It follows reports that officers had descended at the Royal British Legion in Sutton, near Ely, on Saturday (November 21). In an update today, Cambridgeshire Police confirmed it attended the Brookland Centre and arrested two boys. A 15-year-old boy from St Ives has since been charged with taking a vehicle without consent, theft, and possession of a knife. He is also accused of driving without a licence or insurance and is due to appear at Huntingdon Magistrates’ Court on February 3, 2026. A 17-year-old boy from Ely has since been charged with two counts of theft. He is due to appear at Cambridge Magistrates’ Court on January 14, 2026, a spokesperson for the force confirmed. metadata.title: Huntingdon men urged to register with a GP and seek help early this Movember
metadata.contentSnippet: Priory Fields Surgery is urging men to prioritise their health this Movember by registering with a GP and getting any concerns checked early.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Huntingdon men urged to register with a GP and seek help early this Movember
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Priory Fields Surgery is urging men to prioritise their health this Movember by registering with a GP and getting any concerns checked early. The Huntingdon practice is calling on men across the town and surrounding villages to take action, especially during Movember, which raises awareness of prostate cancer, testicular cancer, mental health and suicide prevention. In the UK, one in eight men will be diagnosed with prostate cancer in their lifetime, rising to one in four for Black men. Dr Chris Smith, GP partner at Priory Fields Surgery, said: "Too many men wait until something is really wrong before they come and see us. "We'd much rather see you early, when we can help most. "Whether it's a quick blood pressure check, a worry you've been putting off or how you're feeling in yourself, please don't sit on it. "And if you're not registered with a GP yet, now is the time to do it. "It only takes a few minutes, and you can even contact us online without picking up the phone." The surgery highlighted that men are generally less likely than women to see a GP and often delay seeking help until symptoms become more serious. Early prostate cancer often shows no symptoms, so men over 50, those with a family history of the disease, and Black men are especially encouraged to speak to their GP about their risk. Men are also advised not to ignore changes such as a lump in the testicles, altered toilet habits, unexplained weight loss or persistent tiredness. Regular blood pressure checks are also important, as high blood pressure usually has no symptoms. The surgery is currently welcoming new patients from Huntingdon and nearby villages. Registration can be completed online in just a few minutes. Priory Fields also offers the Ask My GP online contact service, allowing patients to reach the practice without needing to call. Meanwhile, Dr Duncan Blake from the surgery has been invited to discuss men's health on Ouse Valley Radio’s Over to You programme. To register, visit www.prioryfieldssurgery.nhs.uk/practice-information/new-patients.

metadata.title: World’s largest AI breast cancer trial launches in Cambridgeshire
metadata.contentSnippet: Cambridgeshire is the first UK location to launch a major AI-assisted NHS breast screening trial involving 700,000 women.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: World’s largest AI breast cancer trial launches in Cambridgeshire
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A landmark Cambridgeshire trial is testing whether artificial intelligence can detect breast cancer earlier. The study, funded by the National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR), will involve around 700,000 women at 30 sites and is the world’s largest of its kind. The trial will test an AI tool that helps specialists review mammograms. Health Secretary Yvette Cooper launched the study during a visit to Addenbrooke’s Hospital. Patient Shirley meeting Yvette Cooper, Secretary of State for Health and Social Care (Image: Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust/Mel Yeneralski) Ms Cooper said: "This is the biggest AI breast cancer trial in the world, backed by £10 million of government investment to speed up diagnosis and potentially deliver life-saving improvements. "If successful, this technology could help women get a breast cancer diagnosis and start treatment much more quickly, giving them the best possible chance of recovery." Women aged 50 to 71 across the UK are invited for breast screening every three years, with around 2.1 million screenings each year. Two specialist radiologists review each mammogram, although fewer than one per cent show signs of cancer. A set of mammogram images showing a pair of breasts from two different angles. The black and white image has been annotated by the AI tool to indicate where cancer may be. (Image: The EDITH team) The EDITH trial will use the AI tool alongside clinicians to spot cancers that might otherwise be missed because they are too small. If successful, the tool could mean some mammograms need only one radiologist’s review, freeing clinicians to focus on diagnosis and patient care. Shirley, 70, from Cambridgeshire, welcomed the trial after a routine screening found her early-stage breast cancer in October 2025, although she is not taking part. Shirley outside Addenbrooke’s Hospital. (Image: Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust/Mel Yeneralski) She said: "I feel so lucky my cancer was detected early. "When I received the invitation to attend, I had no symptoms and no clue anything was wrong. "My routine mammogram saved my life, so anything that helps other people get diagnosed earlier is crucial. "That's why this trial is so important." Shirley at the cancer screening van in Trumpington, Cambridge where she has the screening scan that diagnosed her breast cancer in 2025. (Image: Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust/Mel Yeneralski) The AI tool will not change the screening appointment, but it may change how the images are reviewed. All mammograms will continue to be reviewed by at least one human radiologist. Professor Fiona Gilbert, from the Department of Radiology at the University of Cambridge and an honorary consultant at Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, said: "Millions of women have a mammogram each year, and fewer than one in 100 will be diagnosed with cancer. "EDITH will test whether an AI-assisted mammogram-reading tool can help experts review images more efficiently, while maintaining professional oversight and the standards women expect from NHS breast screening." Professor Sian Taylor-Phillips, NIHR research professor and professor of population health at the University of Warwick, said: "EDITH will test whether AI can assist NHS staff improve the service for women attending the NHS Breast Screening Programme. "AI-assisted technology could support staff by flagging areas of a mammogram where cancer might be missed to improve early cancer detection." Yvette Cooper, Secretary of State for Health and Social Care finds out how AI is used in the EDITH trial from co-leads Professor Fiona Gilbert (left) and Professor Sian Taylor-Phillips (right). (Image: Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust/Mel Yeneralski) Details of the trial will be included in screening invitation letters, along with information on how to opt out. The trial is a collaboration between the NIHR, NHS England and the UK National Screening Committee. Professor Kevin Dunbar, deputy director of public health, England, said: "The NHS Breast Screening Programme is continuing to modernise, and we are looking carefully at how technology developed using artificial intelligence could support the reading of mammograms safely and effectively. "EDITH will help build the evidence we need, while ensuring patient safety, quality and the expertise of screening professionals remain at the heart of the programme." As the trial expands, it will use AIR-SP, an AI research screening platform funded by nearly £6 million from the government. The study supports the NHS 10 Year Health Plan and the National Cancer Plan’s aims.

metadata.title: Trial to start for inmate charged with murdering Ian Huntley
metadata.contentSnippet: An inmate is due to stand trial charged with the prison murder of Soham killer Ian Huntley, who died after an attack at HMP Frankland

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Trial to start for inmate charged with murdering Ian Huntley
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: An inmate is due to stand trial charged with the prison murder of Soham killer Ian Huntley. Anthony Russell, 44, will go on trial on Monday at Newcastle Crown Court for the alleged murder of the child killer who died following an attack at HMP Frankland, near Durham. Russell is charged with a single offence of murdering the 52-year-old, who was allegedly attacked with a metal bar in a workshop at the maximum security jail on February 26. Huntley was taken to the Royal Victoria Infirmary in Newcastle, where he died on March 7. The trial is estimated to last five days. Huntley was serving a life sentence for the 2002 murders of 10-year-olds Holly Wells and Jessica Chapman. The ex-school caretaker killed the best friends after they left a family barbecue to buy sweets in Soham, Cambridgeshire, on August 4 2002. He dumped their bodies in a ditch 10 miles away. They were not found for 13 days despite a search involving hundreds of police officers. At the time, Huntley lived with Maxine Carr who was a teaching assistant at Holly and Jessica’s primary school. He denied murdering the girls but was convicted after a trial at the Old Bailey in 2003. He was jailed for life with a recommended minimum term of 40 years. Have you got a story you want to share? metadata.title: East of England Ambulance Service wins award for life-saving cardiac arrest video
metadata.contentSnippet: The East of England Ambulance Service has won a national award for its life-saving use of video technology.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: East of England Ambulance Service wins award for life-saving cardiac arrest video
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: The East of England Ambulance Service has won a national award for its life-saving use of video technology. The service received the Digitising Patient Care Award at the HSJ Awards for its Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest Desk, which uses video calls to connect advanced paramedics with people at the scene of a cardiac arrest. This technology allows clinicians to offer real-time guidance before ambulance crews arrive, supporting CPR delivery, defibrillator use, and immediate care through a secure video link sent to a caller's smartphone. Dr Simon Walsh, medical director at the East of England Ambulance Service (EEAST), said: "Winning this award is wonderful recognition for a project that is helping save lives and supporting people during some of the most challenging moments they will ever face. "Every minute matters when someone suffers a cardiac arrest. "This technology allows our clinicians to see what is happening and support people at the scene before our crews arrive. "It helps us improve the care patients receive during the critical first minutes of a cardiac arrest and gives rescuers the confidence to act." EEAST was the first ambulance service in the UK to introduce the video system, doing so in 2025. The service has already supported 913 cardiac arrest incidents during its first 71 shifts, conducted 214 live video assessments, and recorded 421 improvements to resuscitation efforts. It has also prevented the unnecessary dispatch of 113 rapid response vehicles, 424 ambulances, and 228 managerial responses. The project was developed by EEAST and funded by the East of England Ambulance Service Charity through a £142,000 grant from NHS Charities Together, in partnership with Omaze. It has also received support from Essex & Herts Air Ambulance. The technology, powered by the GoodSAM Instant on Scene platform, is already attracting interest from other UK and international ambulance services. Dr Walsh said: "This award reflects the hard work of colleagues across EEAST, our partners at Essex & Herts Air Ambulance, and everyone who has helped develop the service, including the East of England Ambulance Service Charity and NHS Charities Together. "We are proud to see the impact it is having for patients and pleased that other ambulance services are now looking at how they can adopt similar approaches."

metadata.title: Alconbury Weald kicks off Christmas with festive market and Santa
metadata.contentSnippet: Alconbury Weald Christmas Market returns on November 28 with crafts, food, live music, Santa’s grotto and family fun, supporting the local Hardship Fund event.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Alconbury Weald kicks off Christmas with festive market and Santa
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Residents and visitors are invited to kick-start the festive season at Alconbury Weald later this month. The Alconbury Weald Christmas Market will take over the neighbourhood on Saturday, November 28, with food, crafts, live music and family fun. Natalie Leigh-Brown, senior community development lead for Alconbury Weald master developer Urban&Civic, said: "Alconbury Weald Christmas Market is a highlight of the annual events calendar, and a wonderful way to start the festive period. Locals enjoying the Christmas market. (Image: Tim George) "A huge thank you to the organisers, volunteers, Santa’s helpers—John Adams for the presents, Co-op for the wrapping paper and the Tuesday Club who wrapped the presents—the stallholders and everyone involved in creating such a special community event. "We look forward to welcoming residents, family, friends and visitors from surrounding villages and the wider area." The market, organised by the Alconbury Weald Community Association and Urban&Civic, will feature handmade crafts and gifts, toys, festive flowers, hampers and seasonal food including honey, preserves, cheese, baked goods and gin. Alconbury Weald residents enjoying the market. (Image: Tim George) Food trucks and stalls will serve jacket potatoes, hog roast and Lebanese street food, while The Watch Office Bar & Kitchen will offer Yorkshire pudding wraps, mulled wine and other festive drinks. Children from Ermine Street Church Academy will perform carols at 2.30pm, followed by live music from David Piccara between 3.30pm and 5.30pm. Alconbury Weald Christmas Market 2025. (Image: Tim George) Conor Walker will close the evening with a set of festive favourites starting at 6pm. Santa will greet children in a pop-up grotto from 2pm to 6pm, hear their Christmas wishes and hand out presents donated by John Adams, a British toy and games company based at Alconbury Weald Enterprise Campus. Santa listening to the Christmas wishes of children at the Alconbury Weald Christmas market. (Image: Tim George) Grotto places are limited and must be booked in advance. The Alconbury Weald Community Association will also run a stall offering free Christmas crafts for children and a raffle. Christmas baubles will be sold to raise money for the Hardship Fund, which helps residents facing unexpected financial difficulty or the rising cost of living.

metadata.title: £1.85m construction training centre set to open in St Neots in 2027
metadata.contentSnippet: Work has begun on a £1.85m St Neots construction training centre, offering key trade courses and opening in spring 2027 for local Cambridgeshire learners.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: £1.85m construction training centre set to open in St Neots in 2027
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Work has begun on a new £1.85 million construction training centre set to open in Cambridgeshire in spring 2027. The Eastern Education Group (EEG) will run the St Neots Construction Training Centre, offering flexible courses that meet the construction industry’s needs locally. The centre is being built on Cambridge Road at the heart of the St Neots East Expansion, on land provided by master developer Urban and Civic. Rebecca Britton (Urban and Civic), Phil Stittle (Eastern Education Group) and CPCA Mayor Paul Bristow. (Image: Eastern Education Group) Laraine Moody, executive group principal for EEG, said: "We are absolutely thrilled to have the opportunity to support people living in and around St Neots and Cambridgeshire via the creation of this state-of-the-art facility. "This centre follows on from the successful launch of our North Cambridgeshire Training Facility in Chatteris which has gone on to support the community and thousands of students and apprentices since opening in 2022. "Construction courses require specialist teaching spaces, workshops, equipment and safe working environments that cannot always be effectively delivered within traditional classroom settings." St Neots Training Centre - architect image by Dragon Heart Homes. (Image: Eastern Education Group) The centre will offer courses in carpentry and joinery, brickwork, groundwork, plumbing, and electrical installation, along with supporting subjects such as health and safety, site awareness, and sustainability. The 980-square-metre centre will include classrooms, staff offices, student breakout areas and indoor and outdoor training zones. Paul Bristow, Mayor of the Cambridgeshire & Peterborough Combined Authority (CPCA), said: "Real regional growth starts with giving local people the skills to build it. "Turning the turf on this new £1.85 million facility in St Neots is a brilliant milestone that will equip residents with practical, high-value construction trades right in the heart of a growing community." The centre is part of EEG’s new Construction Training Excellence Centre (CTEC) designation, which the group says makes it the only one of its kind in the East of England. Phil Stittle at the launch of the new construction training centre in St Neots. (Image: Eastern Education Group) Tom Sanderson, Executive Councillor for Planning at Huntingdonshire District Council, said: "The St Neots Construction Training Centre is an investment in the future of Huntingdonshire. "By developing the skills local people need to access rewarding careers in construction, we're helping to support economic growth and create opportunities for residents for years to come." The project has been funded by the Cambridgeshire & Peterborough Combined Authority, Huntingdonshire District Council, and Urban and Civic. Dragonheart Homes, Zed Pods and Lindum Group will design and build the centre, with support from Constructed Pathways. The centre is due to be completed in spring 2027.

metadata.title: Peterborough burger restaurant named top-rated on Tripadvisor with 4.9 score
metadata.contentSnippet: A Cambridgeshire burger restaurant has earned almost perfect reviews from customers, with diners praising its food and friendly service.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Peterborough burger restaurant named top-rated on Tripadvisor with 4.9 score
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A Cambridgeshire burger restaurant has earned almost perfect reviews from customers, with diners praising its food and friendly service. Higgsy’s is Peterborough’s top-rated restaurant on Tripadvisor, with a 4.9 rating from hundreds of diners. The burger restaurant, at Fortune Buildings in Cowgate, is rated 4.9 out of five from 286 reviews on Tripadvisor. The website places Higgsy’s first among 469 restaurants in Peterborough. It lists the business under American, fast food and street food. Higgsy’s describes itself on its Tripadvisor listing as a smash burger company and the “home of the Redneck burger”. Its high ratings are also recorded by Restaurant Guru. The website reports a 4.9 out of five Google rating based on 341 reviews. It gives Higgsy’s a score of 4.8 out of five from more than 1,000 votes. Recent customers have praised the food and service. One Google reviewer called their meal the “BEST burger in Peterborough”, while another said everyone in their group gave the restaurant “10 out of 10”. The menu includes the Redneck Burger, other burgers, fried chicken and loaded fries. An online menu listing describes the Redneck Burger as a double smash burger with bacon, a beef frankfurter, onions and melted cheese. The restaurant offers takeaway and eating in. Its listings also mention reservations and outdoor seating. It is open from noon to 4pm and 5.30pm to 9pm from Tuesdays to Thursdays. On Fridays and Saturdays, it is listed as open from noon to 9pm. Higgsy’s is closed on Sundays and Mondays. Tripadvisor categorises the restaurant as serving American, fast food and street food, while the business presents itself as a smash burger company. The reported scores place Higgsy’s among Peterborough’s highest-rated restaurants on the review websites. Higgsy’s also trades from a layby on London Road in Yaxley, where it appealed for permission to continue operating after highway safety concerns were raised.

Autumn
2026
Ramsey Town Council
Residents Communication
RAMSEY COMMUNITIES NEIGHBOURHOOD PLAN
A further step forward
The Ramsey Communities Neighbourhood Plan has been prepared with local voices at the heart. People
gave their opinions via consultation over the summer of 2025 and the plan was then put together by a
steering group of residents before going back out as a draft for further consultation. We’re pleased to say
that it has also passed another significant step - Independent Assessment.
Further details can be found on the Ramsey Town Council website.
What happens next?
The next major step will be a community vote
through a referendum organised by
Huntingdonshire District Council, likely to be in
December 2026. It will be organised in the same
way as an election and everyone on the electoral
register will be notified. You will be asked whether
you accept the Neighbourhood Plan - yes or no.
We will produce a quick reference guide for anyone
who may not have time to read the full document.
Key points include:
Providing new infrastructure, facilities and
services so new development benefits existing,
new and future residents.
Supporting a vibrant community with places to
live, work, stay and play, including affordable
housing and housing with a local connection.
Protecting the historic environment, heritage
assets and green spaces that matter to the
community.
Having our Neighbourhood Plan in place will mean Ramsey
receives 25% of developer contributions rather than the
current 15%.
That means more money can be spent directly in our
community.
neighbourhood.plan@ramseytowncouncil.gov.uk

CIL - Community Infrastructure Levy
What is CIL? Community Infrastructure Levy, commonly referred to as CIL, is money collected by
Huntingdonshire District Council from certain new developments. The funding is then used to help
provide or improve infrastructure needed as communities grow.
The money collected is broadly divided into three areas:
Up to 5% can be retained by Huntingdonshire District Council towards the administration and
collection of CIL.
15% is normally allocated to the Town or Parish Council for the area where the development takes
place. Once an adopted Neighbourhood Plan is in place, this increases to 25%.
Most of the remaining funding is retained by Huntingdonshire District Council for larger strategic
infrastructure projects across the district.
Ramsey Town Council currently receives the 15% neighbourhood portion. Once the Ramsey
Communities Neighbourhood Plan is adopted, this will increase to 25%, giving the Council a greater
share of money from qualifying development to invest back into our communities.
Current projects supported or earmarked through Ramsey Town Council’s CIL funding include:
Improvements at The Moorings.
Contributions towards Local Highways Improvement projects.
Improvements to Newtown Road Play Park.
Improvements to the public toilets.
New benches at the skate park.
CCTV at The Moorings and New Road.
The Double Yellow Lines project.
The Town Council is also considering future projects, including additional parking behind the doctor’s
surgery at Mews Close.
Local Highways Initiative Bid (LHI): what is an LHI?
The Local Highway Improvement programme allows local councils and community organisations to
apply to Cambridgeshire County Council for funding towards highway improvements. Projects can
include new or extended footpaths, traffic-calming measures, speed-reduction schemes, and other
changes designed to improve road and pedestrian safety.
Ramsey Town Council identifies potential projects and submits applications to Cambridgeshire County
Council. Applications are assessed by the County Council and, if successful, funding is awarded
towards the cost of the scheme. Under the current scheme, up to £25,000 can be awarded towards
more complex projects, with applicants expected to contribute at least 10% of the overall cost.
One recent LHI project was the extension of the footpath along Stocking Fen Road towards the
industrial estate, improving pedestrian access for people travelling to and from work. The Council has
also submitted an application for speed-reduction measures on the approach to Ramsey St Mary’s and
is awaiting the outcome.
Abbey College Road Safety Campaign
Abbey College students are raising funds towards the £10,000 needed to help
pay for speed reduction measures on Hollow Lane. Students have been
campaigning, the school submitted an LHI bid, and speed cushions are
planned. They would be grateful if you could spare the price of a coffee and
scan the QR code.

Message from the Mayor of Ramsey
Hello everyone, I hope you’ve all had a wonderful summer. Personally, I can’t
believe how quickly this year has flown by and that, as I write this, we’re already
going into autumn. 
I want to use this column to recognise some amazing people - the Ramsey
Town Council staff team, led by our Clerk, Lisa Renfree. They have had an
incredibly busy summer, with lots of change and new initiatives to contend with
as our Council grows and new Councillors come on board with the ambition to
achieve and deliver more for our residents.
They organised the Bands on the Green programme, delivered a family fun day at QEII Park with
entertainment from the Blues Brothers and Queen tribute acts, produced and managed delivery of our
newsletters to 5,000 homes, and got to grips with a new finance system. This was all on top of day-to-
day customer service and administration, room bookings, council meetings and communications. They
also stepped up to help coordinate meals and drinks for firefighters at Holme Fen during the recent
wildfire, when the RRT Charity had to leave after a week.
They do all of this professionally and with a smile. More often, however, they are facing abusive
behaviour and, as a Council, this is something we will not tolerate. We have had to notify the police
and use CCTV as evidence. Thankfully, this behaviour comes from a minority, and I know many of you
appreciate the time our staff takes to assist you. So, from me and all fellow Councillors: thank you Lisa,
Amanda, Kay, Alison, Quincy, Morgan and Paul - you are appreciated. Keep up the great work for our
community.
Thank you, Ramsey Parish community and beyond
On behalf of Ramsey Town Council, we would like to thank
everyone who supported the firefighters responding to the fire at
Holme Fen. The response from local businesses, organisations
and volunteers was incredible. Our thanks go to The Farmers
Coffee Shop, Gorilla Pizza and Friar Tuck Fish & Chips for
providing food and support; Ramsey Community Centre for
opening its kitchen to prepare the large quantity of meals needed;
The Admiral Wells for becoming a hub of activity, preparing meals
and acting as a donation drop-off point; and Stevelyn & Creative
Crafters for also providing a collection point, to name just a few.
We would also like to thank the many volunteers who gave their time to prepare food and help
wherever needed, as well as everyone who made donations. The JustGiving appeal raised an amazing
£4,546.56. The Mayor also had the privilege of meeting The Duke of Gloucester during his visit to
Holme Fen, where he saw the devastation caused by the fire and personally thanked firefighters, the
owners of The Admiral Wells and local volunteers for their incredible efforts.
The Lord-Lieutenant, Julie Spence, who accompanied him, spoke of how proud
she was to see the community come together so quickly and effectively.
Firefighters expressed their appreciation for every meal, drink and homemade
cake provided during the response.
Following the fire, a meeting of local community groups has been arranged for 1
October to discuss emergency planning and how the community can work
together in response to future major incidents.

Meet the new Town Council members
My husband and I chose Ramsey 26 years ago based on what we felt it had to
offer us as a family and our growing children: the wonderful people, the community,
the facilities, the coffee shops, the leisure centre and the parks. There have been
many changes since then, and I want to make sure Ramsey remains that
wonderful place. Hopefully, my role as a magistrate, my previous experience with
numerous community groups and the experience of raising my children in this
community will stand me in good stead to help the people of Ramsey further.
If you have opinions about the community in which you live, then for me, it is
important to express them in a positive way by becoming involved in the decision-
making forums and involving yourself actively and practically in the implementation
of ideas. In addition, having benefited from living in Ramsey for many years, I also
felt that it was time to repay some of those benefits by contributing, in some small
part, to the development of our community. I therefore took a leap of faith earlier
this year and put my name forward for election to the town council.
 
My family and I moved to Ramsey two years ago, and what began as a new
chapter has become home. With my daughter attending school locally, I have seen
how important a connected, inclusive community is. I want her to grow up
somewhere people feel proud to call home. Throughout my career, including my
recent role in strategic transformation and programme management at M&S, I have
developed strong skills in collaboration, listening and turning ideas into action. I
want to bring these values to Ramsey, listening to residents and supporting our
town’s continued growth. Please say hello and share your thoughts when you see
me around town. 
Freedom of the Town – Pat Taylor
Freedom of the Town is the highest honour a Town Council can
award. On Sunday 20th September 2026, it was awarded to Pat
Taylor for her commitment to Ramsey.
Pat was an English teacher for many years and has taught lots of
residents; however, her volunteering means that she is also
known in many other capacities, spread across the years.
She was a Trustee of Ramsey Welfare Charities and Jones
Court, supporting our older residents; she volunteered at the
foodbank, where Reverend Richard Darmody said her help and
support were invaluable.
Council meeting dates - All residents are welcome
Ramsey Town Council meets on the second Thursday of every month at 7 pm in the Council Building
on Great Whyte. Residents are welcome to listen and have an opportunity at the start of the meeting to
address Council members.
8 October · 12 November · 10 December · 14 January · 11 February · 11 March
8 April · 13 May (AGM) · 10 June · 8 July · 12 August · 9 September
Pat was part of the steering committee that helped to form Ramsey U3A, and she was the first Chair
from 2011 to 2012, remaining a member to the present day.
She has also been a Town Councillor, serving for 26 years until her recent retirement, and has been
Mayor of Ramsey twice.
Her nomination for the Freedom of Ramsey was put forward by Cllr Adela Costello and was
wholeheartedly approved by fellow Councillors. Our congratulations to Pat; thank you for all you have
done to support our community.
Cllr Webster
Cllr Axelsen
Cllr Thompson

Public Toilets - New Road
The Moorings
It has been lovely to see residents and young people making use of
the improvements at The Moorings, including young people fishing
and spending time with friends.
Ramsey Town Council is also working with Ramsey Rotary to
introduce crocuses and other planting to bring more colour to the
area. The improvements at The Moorings have been funded through
the Community Infrastructure Levy (CIL). 
Ramsey Town Council is currently replacing the doors at the public toilets and has installed a payment
facility, which will come into operation once the refurbishment works are complete. The Council has
decided to introduce a small charge for use of the facilities to reduce anti-social behaviour and help
ensure the toilets remain clean and in good condition. CCTV will also be installed on New Road to help
identify those responsible for anti-social behaviour and to support Huntingdonshire District Council and
the police in dealing with incidents.
Skate Park Benches and No to Floodlights
As we go to print, the Council is selecting and arranging new picnic benches to be installed near the
skate park, ready for spring 2027. These, together with the new concrete rumble-strip area, are
expected to be in place in October and some grass seeding will continue to improve the area for young
people and residents.
There has recently been incorrect information circulating on social media suggesting that the Council is
considering floodlighting at the skate park. This is not the case. When the Council agreed to the skate
park, it was clear that the facility should not be encouraged for use after dark. This also reflects
feedback from nearby residents who have contacted the Clerk and Councillors with concerns about the
potential for increased anti-social behaviour during the evening.
Newtown Road Under-5s Play Park Improvement
Residents will have seen that the new fencing to extend the under-5s play area has now been
completed. The public consultation has also been launched and shared with residents and nurseries
across the Ramsey area. Ramsey Town Council has listened to feedback from families with young
children about the limited amount of play equipment currently available and the need to update the
existing facilities.
With a growing number of young families in the area, the Council felt it was important to make
Newtown Road Play Park a priority, particularly as other play parks across the town have benefited
from new equipment over the last three years.

Bands on the Green 2026
Bands on the Green has been really successful. The
weather was very kind to us - sometimes almost too hot!
It was good to have some new bands join us this year,
including the Abbey College Band and Janine Mitchell
singing. Ramsey Town Council would like to thank the
team of volunteers at St Thomas a Becket Church for
supplying teas, coffee and scrumptious cake.
Heritage Day - Sunday 13 September
Heritage Day was very popular this year, and it
was wonderful to meet people from as far away as
Berkshire and Essex. The Heritage Partnership
funded reenactments of the Vikings, the Sealed
Knot, and the Romans. Luckily, the Mayor
survived the stocks!
Heritage Day showcases our history: Ramsey Rural Museum, Victorian Walled Garden, Abbey
Gatehouse, St Thomas a Becket Church and the Mortuary Chapels.
The Hangout - Youth Club every Thursday
Ramsey Neighbourhoods Trust has launched its youth club, The
Hangout. It is open to all young people aged 11+ and is held at
the Pavilion on Cricketfield Lane. The youth club is open from
6.15pm to 7.45pm every Thursday during term time. Ramsey
Town Council is pleased to fund the youth club.
Youth Café has opened again and runs every Monday from
3.30pm to 6pm at The Farmers Café. It is free to attend, tuck is
available, and it provides a safe place to hang out with friends.
BOSH is the club for younger people. It is held every Thursday during term time from 4.30pm to 6pm,
offering children fun and games.

Rotary in Ramsey
Anti-Social Behaviour - How to Report
Ramsey Town Council has recently received several requests for CCTV cameras in different areas of
the community following concerns about anti-social behaviour.
Reports of anti-social behaviour should be made to Huntingdonshire District Council. Reporting
incidents is important because it helps build an accurate picture of where problems are occurring and
provides the evidence needed for the relevant authorities to take action.
Anti-social behaviour can be reported online at:
forms.huntingdonshire.gov.uk/REPORTANTISOCIALBEHAVIOUR/launch
Alternatively, email communityaction@huntingdonshire.gov.uk or call 01480 388388.
One-to-one meeting with a Councillor
If you would like to speak to a Councillor on a one-to-one basis about a local
issue, concern, or idea, appointments can be arranged throughout the week,
including evenings and weekends.
This allows residents to discuss matters directly with a Councillor at a time
that is convenient for them.
Simply scan the QR code, complete the short form and request an
appointment. A suitable time can then be arranged with you.
Ramsey Business Forum
Ramsey Town Council is launching its first Business Forum on Tuesday 13 October at 6pm at The
George, Ramsey. 
The forum will give local businesses a direct opportunity to raise concerns, share ideas, and help
shape the Council’s new Economic Development work, focused on increasing footfall and supporting
local businesses.
All Businesses are welcome.
Ramsey Town Council is pleased to continue its close
relationship with Rotary in Ramsey. The Clerk and Rotary’s
Secretary regularly meet to share information and work
together on events.
The Council looks forward to hosting one of the Santa Float evenings
for the volunteers after they have been out raising funds.
To get involved, contact
secretary@ramseyrotary.co.uk and book to
attend the planning evening on Wednesday 11
November.
Look out for the Santa Tracker to find
out when he will visit your street.

Raising funds for the Mayor’s
charities: Ramsey Rural Museum and
the Armed Services Veterans
Breakfast Club.
No experience is needed - trust the
process and you will have loads of fun
and create a wonderful item.
Click the QR code to book or email
events@ramseytowncouncil.gov.uk
.
Events for you to come along and enjoy
Scan the QR code
to donate. Every
pound is very much
appreciated.
Ramsey Christmas Lights is putting the
tree up on Saturday 14 November.
Complete the festive trail to collect your
bauble, decorate it and have it hung on the
tree. That afternoon there will be a children’s
Christmas Party, a chance to have a family
photograph taken by a professional
photographer, Santa in his grotto for a selfie
and a Snow Globe. The party is free and will
be held at Ramsey Community Centre, with
refreshments on sale.
Switch-On Day - Saturday 28 November. The morning
starts at 10am at Abbey College with the Christmas
Bazaar. The town-centre switch-on starts at 3pm with a
Taylor Swift tribute, and the lights go on at 5.15pm. The
fairground will be in town until 8pm. There is an envelope
with this newsletter, or you can scan the QR code above.
Festive Markets
Saturday 5 December
Saturday 12 December
Saturday 19 December
To book a stall, contact:
events@ramseytowncouncil.gov.uk
Festive Extravaganza
Saturday 12 December, 9am-1pm
Come and join Santa, make a free gift and see
who might visit!

I therefore took a leap of faith earlier this year and put my name forward for election to the town council.

My family and I moved to Ramsey two years ago, and what began as a new chapter has become home. With my daughter attending school locally, I have seen how important a connected, inclusive community is. I want her to grow up somewhere people feel proud to call home. Throughout my career, including my recent role in strategic transformation and programme management at M&S, I have developed strong skills in collaboration, listening and turning ideas into action. I want to bring these values to Ramsey, listening to residents and supporting our town’s continued growth. Please say hello and share your thoughts when you see me around town. Freedom of the Town – Pat Taylor Freedom of the Town is the highest honour a Town Council can award. On Sunday 20th September 2026, it was awarded to Pat Taylor for her commitment to Ramsey. Pat was an English teacher for many years and has taught lots of residents; however, her volunteering means that she is also known in many other capacities, spread across the years. She was a Trustee of Ramsey Welfare Charities and Jones Court, supporting our older residents; she volunteered at the foodbank, where Reverend Richard Darmody said her help and support were invaluable. Council meeting dates - All residents are welcome Ramsey Town Council meets on the second Thursday of every month at 7 pm in the Council Building on Great Whyte. Residents are welcome to listen and have an opportunity at the start of the meeting to address Council members. 8 October · 12 November · 10 December · 14 January · 11 February · 11 March 8 April · 13 May (AGM) · 10 June · 8 July · 12 August · 9 September Pat was part of the steering committee that helped to form Ramsey U3A, and she was the first Chair from 2011 to 2012, remaining a member to the present day. She has also been a Town Councillor, serving for 26 years until her recent retirement, and has been Mayor of Ramsey twice. Her nomination for the Freedom of Ramsey was put forward by Cllr Adela Costello and was wholeheartedly approved by fellow Councillors. Our congratulations to Pat; thank you for all you have done to support our community. Cllr Webster Cllr Axelsen Cllr Thompson

Public Toilets - New Road The Moorings It has been lovely to see residents and young people making use of the improvements at The Moorings, including young people fishing and spending time with friends. Ramsey Town Council is also working with Ramsey Rotary to introduce crocuses and other planting to bring more colour to the area. The improvements at The Moorings have been funded through the Community Infrastructure Levy (CIL). Ramsey Town Council is currently replacing the doors at the public toilets and has installed a payment facility, which will come into operation once the refurbishment works are complete. The Council has decided to introduce a small charge for use of the facilities to reduce anti-social behaviour and help ensure the toilets remain clean and in good condition. CCTV will also be installed on New Road to help identify those responsible for anti-social behaviour and to support Huntingdonshire District Council and the police in dealing with incidents. Skate Park Benches and No to Floodlights As we go to print, the Council is selecting and arranging new picnic benches to be installed near the skate park, ready for spring 2027. These, together with the new concrete rumble-strip area, are expected to be in place in October and some grass seeding will continue to improve the area for young people and residents. There has recently been incorrect information circulating on social media suggesting that the Council is considering floodlighting at the skate park. This is not the case. When the Council agreed to the skate park, it was clear that the facility should not be encouraged for use after dark. This also reflects feedback from nearby residents who have contacted the Clerk and Councillors with concerns about the potential for increased anti-social behaviour during the evening. Newtown Road Under-5s Play Park Improvement Residents will have seen that the new fencing to extend the under-5s play area has now been completed. The public consultation has also been launched and shared with residents and nurseries across the Ramsey area. Ramsey Town Council has listened to feedback from families with young children about the limited amount of play equipment currently available and the need to update the existing facilities. With a growing number of young families in the area, the Council felt it was important to make Newtown Road Play Park a priority, particularly as other play parks across the town have benefited from new equipment over the last three years.

Bands on the Green 2026 Bands on the Green has been really successful. The weather was very kind to us - sometimes almost too hot! It was good to have some new bands join us this year, including the Abbey College Band and Janine Mitchell singing. Ramsey Town Council would like to thank the team of volunteers at St Thomas a Becket Church for supplying teas, coffee and scrumptious cake. Heritage Day - Sunday 13 September Heritage Day was very popular this year, and it was wonderful to meet people from as far away as Berkshire and Essex. The Heritage Partnership funded reenactments of the Vikings, the Sealed Knot, and the Romans. Luckily, the Mayor survived the stocks! Heritage Day showcases our history: Ramsey Rural Museum, Victorian Walled Garden, Abbey Gatehouse, St Thomas a Becket Church and the Mortuary Chapels. The Hangout - Youth Club every Thursday Ramsey Neighbourhoods Trust has launched its youth club, The Hangout. It is open to all young people aged 11+ and is held at the Pavilion on Cricketfield Lane. The youth club is open from 6.15pm to 7.45pm every Thursday during term time. Ramsey Town Council is pleased to fund the youth club. Youth Café has opened again and runs every Monday from 3.30pm to 6pm at The Farmers Café. It is free to attend, tuck is available, and it provides a safe place to hang out with friends. BOSH is the club for younger people. It is held every Thursday during term time from 4.30pm to 6pm, offering children fun and games.

Rotary in Ramsey Anti-Social Behaviour - How to Report Ramsey Town Council has recently received several requests for CCTV cameras in different areas of the community following concerns about anti-social behaviour. Reports of anti-social behaviour should be made to Huntingdonshire District Council. Reporting incidents is important because it helps build an accurate picture of where problems are occurring and provides the evidence needed for the relevant authorities to take action. Anti-social behaviour can be reported online at: forms.huntingdonshire.gov.uk/REPORTANTISOCIALBEHAVIOUR/launch Alternatively, email communityaction@huntingdonshire.gov.uk or call 01480 388388. One-to-one meeting with a Councillor If you would like to speak to a Councillor on a one-to-one basis about a local issue, concern, or idea, appointments can be arranged throughout the week, including evenings and weekends. This allows residents to discuss matters directly with a Councillor at a time that is convenient for them. Simply scan the QR code, complete the short form and request an appointment. A suitable time can then be arranged with you. Ramsey Business Forum Ramsey Town Council is launching its first Business Forum on Tuesday 13 October at 6pm at The George, Ramsey. The forum will give local businesses a direct opportunity to raise concerns, share ideas, and help shape the Council’s new Economic Development work, focused on increasing footfall and supporting local businesses. All Businesses are welcome. Ramsey Town Council is pleased to continue its close relationship with Rotary in Ramsey. The Clerk and Rotary’s Secretary regularly meet to share information and work together on events. The Council looks forward to hosting one of the Santa Float evenings for the volunteers after they have been out raising funds. To get involved, contact secretary@ramseyrotary.co.uk and book to attend the planning evening on Wednesday 11 November. Look out for the Santa Tracker to find out when he will visit your street.

Raising funds for the Mayor’s charities: Ramsey Rural Museum and the Armed Services Veterans Breakfast Club. No experience is needed - trust the process and you will have loads of fun and create a wonderful item. Click the QR code to book or email events@ramseytowncouncil.gov.uk . Events for you to come along and enjoy Scan the QR code to donate. Every pound is very much appreciated. Ramsey Christmas Lights is putting the tree up on Saturday 14 November. Complete the festive trail to collect your bauble, decorate it and have it hung on the tree. That afternoon there will be a children’s Christmas Party, a chance to have a family photograph taken by a professional photographer, Santa in his grotto for a selfie and a Snow Globe. The party is free and will be held at Ramsey Community Centre, with refreshments on sale. Switch-On Day - Saturday 28 November. The morning starts at 10am at Abbey College with the Christmas Bazaar. The town-centre switch-on starts at 3pm with a Taylor Swift tribute, and the lights go on at 5.15pm. The fairground will be in town until 8pm. There is an envelope with this newsletter, or you can scan the QR code above. Festive Markets Saturday 5 December Saturday 12 December Saturday 19 December To book a stall, contact: events@ramseytowncouncil.gov.uk Festive Extravaganza Saturday 12 December, 9am-1pm Come and join Santa, make a free gift and see who might visit!

news.content: Autumn 2026 Ramsey Town Council Residents Communication RAMSEY COMMUNITIES NEIGHBOURHOOD PLAN A further step forward The Ramsey Communities Neighbourhood Plan has been prepared with local voices at the heart. People gave their opinions via consultation over the summer of 2025 and the plan was then put together by a steering group of residents before going back out as a draft for further consultation. We’re pleased to say that it has also passed another significant step - Independent Assessment. Further details can be found on the Ramsey Town Council website. What happens next? The next major step will be a community vote through a referendum organised by Huntingdonshire District Council, likely to be in December 2026. It will be organised in the same way as an election and everyone on the electoral register will be notified. You will be asked whether you accept the Neighbourhood Plan - yes or no. We will produce a quick reference guide for anyone who may not have time to read the full document. Key points include: Providing new infrastructure, facilities and services so new development benefits existing, new and future residents. Supporting a vibrant community with places to live, work, stay and play, including affordable housing and housing with a local connection. Protecting the historic environment, heritage assets and green spaces that matter to the community. Having our Neighbourhood Plan in place will mean Ramsey receives 25% of developer contributions rather than the current 15%. That means more money can be spent directly in our community. neighbourhood.plan@ramseytowncouncil.gov.uk

news.content: CIL - Community Infrastructure Levy What is CIL? Community Infrastructure Levy, commonly referred to as CIL, is money collected by Huntingdonshire District Council from certain new developments. The funding is then used to help provide or improve infrastructure needed as communities grow. The money collected is broadly divided into three areas: Up to 5% can be retained by Huntingdonshire District Council towards the administration and collection of CIL. 15% is normally allocated to the Town or Parish Council for the area where the development takes place. Once an adopted Neighbourhood Plan is in place, this increases to 25%. Most of the remaining funding is retained by Huntingdonshire District Council for larger strategic infrastructure projects across the district. Ramsey Town Council currently receives the 15% neighbourhood portion. Once the Ramsey Communities Neighbourhood Plan is adopted, this will increase to 25%, giving the Council a greater share of money from qualifying development to invest back into our communities. Current projects supported or earmarked through Ramsey Town Council’s CIL funding include: Improvements at The Moorings. Contributions towards Local Highways Improvement projects. Improvements to Newtown Road Play Park. Improvements to the public toilets. New benches at the skate park. CCTV at The Moorings and New Road. The Double Yellow Lines project. The Town Council is also considering future projects, including additional parking behind the doctor’s surgery at Mews Close. Local Highways Initiative Bid (LHI): what is an LHI? The Local Highway Improvement programme allows local councils and community organisations to apply to Cambridgeshire County Council for funding towards highway improvements. Projects can include new or extended footpaths, traffic-calming measures, speed-reduction schemes, and other changes designed to improve road and pedestrian safety. Ramsey Town Council identifies potential projects and submits applications to Cambridgeshire County Council. Applications are assessed by the County Council and, if successful, funding is awarded towards the cost of the scheme. Under the current scheme, up to £25,000 can be awarded towards more complex projects, with applicants expected to contribute at least 10% of the overall cost. One recent LHI project was the extension of the footpath along Stocking Fen Road towards the industrial estate, improving pedestrian access for people travelling to and from work. The Council has also submitted an application for speed-reduction measures on the approach to Ramsey St Mary’s and is awaiting the outcome. Abbey College Road Safety Campaign Abbey College students are raising funds towards the £10,000 needed to help pay for speed reduction measures on Hollow Lane. Students have been campaigning, the school submitted an LHI bid, and speed cushions are planned. They would be grateful if you could spare the price of a coffee and scan the QR code.

metadata.title: 'Legendary' cooking competition making 'explosive' return to ITV next year
metadata.contentSnippet: Hell's Kitchen is making a return to ITV next year with Gordon Ramsay coming back to help the 10 celebrity contestants.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: 'Legendary' cooking competition making 'explosive' return to ITV next year
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A “legendary” cooking show is making an “explosive” return to ITV next year with a brand-new series in 2027. Hell’s Kitchen is making a comeback after its last UK series aired in 2009. The cooking competition will see Gordon Ramsay return to the kitchen to mentor the celebrity contestants. The Traitor’s star Claudia Winkleman will be taking on the role of host for the live event. Hell’s Kitchen is set to bring its “signature blend of high-stakes jeopardy and drama, intense personalities and unfiltered reality, out of the kitchen and onto our screens”. There will be a line-up of 10 celebrity contestants from social media creators and entertainment stars to sports personalities and comedians. The celebrities will be expected to deliver Michelin-standard dishes every episode. Alongside Gordon, there will be two new sous chefs and a maître D to help the celebrities with their cooking throughout the series. The live event will see 100 diners including celebrity guests, the contestants’ friends and family, and members of the public testing out the food. Claudia will be guiding the viewers and the VIP guests through the competition. The audience will be given the power to vote off the celebrity contestants who are not performing to the highest standard. Hell’s Kitchen will feature 10 episodes that are each 60 minutes long aired over two weeks and will be packed with “shocking format twists and culinary tasks”. Gordon Ramsay said: “Hell's Kitchen is returning to the UK bigger, bolder, and 100% hotter than ever before. “A brand-new restaurant, an all-star celebrity cast and culinary challenges that will push even the most confident cooks. “With live eliminations, sky-high stakes and no room for excuses, let me be very clear, every service will be a battle, and every plate will make or break their place in the competition.” Claudia Winkleman added: “I am very excited to be joining Gordon for the return of Hell's Kitchen. “It’s fast, thrilling and unpredictable live television. “I can’t wait to guide our viewers through the heat of the kitchen and am really hoping he goes easy on them, and asks for toast.” Will you be watching the new series of Hell's Kitchen? Let us know in the comments.

metadata.title: Will your Christmas present be delivered by the 'UK's worst' courier?
metadata.contentSnippet: Evri are the worst-rated couriers in 2026, according to the 'people's champions' Citizens Advice.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Will your Christmas present be delivered by the 'UK's worst' courier?
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Evri are the worst-rated couriers in 2026, according to the 'people's champions' Citizens Advice. The charity unveiled their annual league table yesterday [November 18], which rates the UK's biggest parcel delivery firms out of five. They're judged on this year's customer experiences across four categories: delivery and collection, accessibility, customer service and trust. The worst-rated courier was Evri, which picked up a 1.75 rating for delivery and collection, 2.2 for accessibility, 2.5 for customer service and 2.2 for trust, totalling an overall score of 2. The best-ranked was Royal Mail, scoring 3 for delivery and collection, 2.7 for accessibility, 2.5 for customer service and a table-high of 4.2 for trust, making a final score of 3. Amazon Logistics came second with an overall score of 2.75 after being rated 2.5 for collection and delivery, 2.5 for accessibility, 3.25 for customer service and 3.9 for trust. DPD and InPost were tied in third on 2.25 stars despite scoring slightly differently in the four tests. DPD scored 2.25 and InPost scored 2.5 for delivery and collection, for accessibility they were rated 2.3 and 2.5, for customer service 1.75 and 1 and then 3 and 2.2 for trust. InPost's 1 out of 5 rating for customer service was the lowest score in that category of all five couriers in the table. The table is part of a wider study which Citizens Advice say reveals that almost a third of parcel recipients in the past month (15 million) faced problems. They add more than a third of those (35%) saw further problems such as 'sluggish' response times or 'frustrating automated systems'. The charity warned that new accessibility requirements 'lack teeth' as they found those with accessibility needs are almost twice as likely to experience issues (45% vs 23%). Dame Clare Moriarty, chief executive of Citizens Advice, said: "Parcel deliveries are an essential part of life yet millions still bear the brunt of the dismal delivery practices normalised for too many years. "This is particularly concerning for people with accessibility needs, who are almost twice as likely to experience problems. "Consumers rarely get to choose their courier, yet they’re the ones left dealing with the consequences when things go wrong and trying to fix problems that shouldn’t be happening in the first place. "It’s clear that Ofcom’s approach isn’t working. "The regulator has the power to strengthen protections for consumers and it must. "It’s the only way to stop delivery standards flatlining and improve the market once and for all." An Evri spokesperson said: "Citizens Advice’s ranking of Evri in joint-second place for customer service out of five operators in its annual league table is testament to the significant investment we continue to make in delivering improvements Including resolving customer issues promptly and effectively. "The ranking also recognises progress in trust and accessibility. "We deliver more than a billion parcels a year and millions every day and continue to invest significantly in providing a strong and reliable service at an enormous scale. "This year alone, we have invested £32.2 million in infrastructure, technology and network capacity. "Independent data from The Despatch Company, covering 1.3 million Evri parcels, found that 99.4% were delivered within seven working days, demonstrating the strong underlying performance of our network. "We are also continuing to make it easier for customers to get support when they need it, while investing in accessibility and greater choice. "More than 200,000 accessibility preferences have now been set by customers, which is more than double the number a year ago, alongside improvements to accessibility information across our ParcelShop and locker network. "Citizen's Advice has also awarded Evri the highest accessibility policy score of all operators assessed which recognises the significant work and investment we continue to make to improve the customer experience. "Overall, we know there is more to do and will continue listening to customers and acting on their feedback. "Our focus remains on continuously improving customer experiences and making practical changes that deliver better outcomes for everyone." A Royal Mail spokesperson said: "We’re pleased to lead Citizens Advice’s Parcels League Table again this year by ranking first for customer trust and for delivery and collection. "As the UK’s postal service, we want everyone to be able to send and receive parcels easily. "We’ve been working to make our services more accessible and ranked first in the new Accessibility League Table but we know there’s more to do, both at Royal Mail and across the industry. "With Christmas approaching, customers are counting on us to get their cards and presents there on time. "We’ve been preparing since January and we’re ready for the extra mail. "In each of the past two years more than 99% of items posted by our last recommended posting dates arrived in time for Christmas and we intend to deliver the same again this year." Amazon, DPD and InPost were all contacted for comment. Ofcom have been contacted for comment.

metadata.title: New publican sought for 'beautiful' and 'characterful' pub in Cambridgeshire
metadata.contentSnippet: A new publican is being sought to take the reins of a "characterful" and much-loved pub in a Cambridgeshire town.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: New publican sought for 'beautiful' and 'characterful' pub in Cambridgeshire
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A new publican is being sought to take the reins of a "characterful" and much-loved pub in a Cambridgeshire town. The White Horse, in Eaton Socon, St Neots, is looking for an experienced operator who can take on the "charming listed building". Stonegate describes the premises as "farm more than a traditional pub operation". It boasts a "substantial commercial kitchen", "versatile internal trading spaces",  "extensive beer garden" and an outdoor bar. The pub also has a bandstand for live entertainment, customer parking and potential letting opportunities. It presents "multiple opportunities to develop a thriving hospital business with several revenue streams". The pub previously operated a highly successful carvery and benefits from a "loyal local following". It also benefits from a roadside location between the A1 and A428, which provides "strong passing trade and access to a growing customer base". Also included is "generous" private accommodation with five bedrooms, two bathrooms, a lounge, kitchen, office and storage room. Katy Jones, regional manager at Stonegate Group, said: “The White Horse is a beautiful, characterful building in a fantastic location with huge potential for the right operator. "We're looking for an experienced publican, ideally with a strong food background, who can build on the pub's excellent reputation. "With its extensive trading space, established food credentials, outdoor facilities and additional income opportunities, The White Horse offers a genuine chance to create a successful multi-faceted hospitality business." Stonegate said it hopes to find an operator who can "build on the pub's strong foundations and help secure its future as a valued community hub for years to come." metadata.title: Accessible doors at GP surgery 'vandalised' days after being installed
metadata.contentSnippet: Staff at The Charles Hicks Centre in Huntingdon have been left "deeply saddened" after a set of automatic doors were "vandalised".

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Accessible doors at GP surgery 'vandalised' days after being installed
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Staff at a doctor's surgery in Cambridgeshire have been left "deeply saddened" after its automatic front doors were "vandalised". The Charles Hicks Centre, in Huntingdon, revealed staff had arrived to discover the doors, which were installed to improve disabled access, had been damaged. The wiring to the doors was "cut" just days after they were installed, in what the surgery has described as a "senseless act". Practice manage, Lisa Harrison, said the incident likely occurred between 6.30pm on Thursday (November 19) and 7.30am the next day. The surgery described the incident as a "senseless act" (Image: The Hicks Group Practice) She added: "The doors have been badly scratched and the wiring has been cut, leaving the automatic entrance completely unusable. "This is a senseless act that directly impacts our most vulnerable patients and diverts vital funds away from patient care to cover the cost of urgent repairs. "We have reported the incident to Cambridgeshire Constabulary and are working closely with engineers to get the doors fixed as quickly as possible. "In the meantime, our team is on hand to help anyone entering the building. "We urge anyone who saw or heard anything suspicious around Ermine Street last night to contact the police." Cambridgeshire Police has been contacted for further information. Have you got a story you want to share? Get in touch at oliver.murphy@newsquest.co.uk

metadata.title: Discover 'spectacular' restaurant named among best in the world
metadata.contentSnippet: If you're looking for Indian restaurant named among the best in the world, then look no further than Olive Naturally Indian in St Neots

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Discover 'spectacular' restaurant named among best in the world
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: If you're looking for an Indian restaurant named among the world's best-reviewed businesses, then look no further. With its "modern decor" and "extensive menu", it is unsurprising Olive Naturally Indian, in Eynesbury, St Neots, has been described as "spectacular". If that wasn't enough, the restaurant received the Trip Advisor Traveller's Choice award in September last year. Reviews from millions of Trip Advisor travellers placed the award-winning venue in the top 10 per cent of restaurants worldwide. On its website, Olive Naturally Indian proudly describes how it offers "authentic and popular" Indian street foods. Manager Abul Chowdhury told The Hunts Post the restaurant continues to "attract large numbers of customers" in spite of the rising cost of living. "This is down to our excellent food, service, and fantastic reviews which show we are not a run-of-the mill restaurant," he said. "We serve authentic Indian street food, which is a completely different umbrella of cuisines in the Indian restaurant sector. "We're well away from the town centre and even in these difficult times we continue to fill our restaurant." Unsurprisingly, Olive Naturally Indian has received raving reviews on Trip Advisor, with visitors praising its "fantastic flavours" and "relaxed atmosphere". One visitor said: "Can honestly say it’s probably the best Indian meal I have ever eaten, flavours were fantastic and portion sizes were spot on. "The staff were very friendly. Will definitely be returning and would fully recommend." Another added: "Warm welcome, lovely food, quality ingredients, tasted flavoursome. Very courteous staff, how customer service should be." Olive Naturally Indian has several other restaurants, including Flitwick, in Bedfordshire, Hemel Hempstead, in Hertfordshire, and Princes Risborough in Buckinghamshire. Earlier this year, the chain opened its fifth restaurant in St Albans, which is also in Hertfordshire. Have you got a story you want to share? metadata.title: The best woodland walks in Cambridgeshire to discover this autumn
metadata.contentSnippet: From ancient woodlands and National Trust estates to wildlife-rich nature reserves, Cambridgeshire offers far more woodland scenery than many people realise.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: The best woodland walks in Cambridgeshire to discover this autumn
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: From ancient woodlands and National Trust estates to wildlife-rich nature reserves, Cambridgeshire offers far more woodland scenery than many people realise. Showcasing some of the county's most attractive forest and woodland walks, here are six beauty spots to discover this autumn. While best known for its wetlands, Wicken Fen also contains areas of woodland and scrub that create a wonderfully varied walking experience. The reserve's network of paths passes through reedbeds, grassland and developing woodland, offering visitors the chance to spot everything from dragonflies and marsh harriers to grazing Konik ponies. The ever-changing landscape and huge skies make every walk feel different, whatever the season. One of the county's most important ancient woodlands, Monk's Wood is a haven for wildlife and a favourite among walkers seeking tranquillity. The reserve's oak and ash trees line peaceful trails that weave through centuries-old woodland. In spring, woodland flowers brighten the forest floor, while birdwatchers can spot woodpeckers, nuthatches and other species. The largest country estate in Cambridgeshire offers far more than historic architecture. Its extensive parkland includes pockets of mature woodland, tree-lined avenues and scenic walking routes stretching across the estate. Visitors can wander beneath ancient trees before emerging into open countryside with far-reaching views. Managed by the National Trust, it combines woodland beauty with some of the county's most impressive landscapes. Famous for its gardens, Anglesey Abbey also boasts beautiful woodland walks that are particularly spectacular during autumn. Shaded paths wind through mature trees and carefully designed landscapes, creating a peaceful retreat from nearby Cambridge. Seasonal colour is a major draw, while the estate's varied habitats support a wide range of birds and other wildlife. It is one of the most picturesque places for a gentle woodland stroll in the county. Covering more than 170 acres, Hinchingbrooke Country Park combines mature woodland with lakes, meadows and open countryside. Well-maintained trails guide visitors through shady woodland areas rich in birdlife and seasonal wildflowers. The park's accessibility and variety of routes make it popular with families, dog walkers and runners alike, while its peaceful setting provides a welcome escape from nearby Huntingdon. One of Cambridgeshire's most diverse nature reserves, Paxton Pits features woodland trails alongside lakes, meadows and wetlands. The reserve is particularly popular with wildlife enthusiasts thanks to its rich birdlife and varied habitats. Visitors can enjoy peaceful woodland walks before exploring the waterside paths and observation points. At Paxton Pits, the Heron Trail and Meadow Trail offer opportunities to spot wildlife around the reserve's lakes as the seasons change. Have you got a story you want to share?
