MINUTES OF RAMSEY TOWN COUNCIL MEETING 
held at 7pm on Thursday 9 July 2026 at  
Ramsey Town Council Great Whyte, Ramsey 
 
 
Present:  Councillors: A Austin, I Axelsen, J Bufton, J Clarke, M Clarke, S Corney (Dep 
Mayor), V Fendley (Mayor), S Fice, C Maskell, R Terrill and L Webster. 
In attendance: Mrs L Renfree, Town Clerk  
 
254. Apologies for Absence. 
Cllrs J Aubin, J Clarke, L Knight, P Rose, and E Welsh. The Clerk informed members that Cllr 
Rebecca Cope had sent in by email her resignation that afternoon. 
 
Cllr V Fendley welcomed Cllr L Webster to her first Full Council meeting. 
  
255.To Receive Declarations of Interest. 
There were no Declarations of Interest. 
 
256. Public Participation. 
There were two members of the public present. 
 
257. Minutes of the Last Meeting to be Approved. 
Having  been proposed  by  Cllr  S  Corney  and  seconded  by  Cllr  M  Clarke,  Council voted 10 
FOR and 1  ABSTENTION for the  Minutes  of  the  meeting  of  25th  June  2026  as  a  correct 
record. 
 
258.  District  Councillor  Update. Cllrs  H  Tobias,  K  Maheshwari  and  R  Coogan  had  been 
invited to address Town Council Members.  
Cllr K Maheshwari had put in his apologies, but no apologies were received by Cllr H Tobias 
or Cllr R Coogan. 
The Clerk read an email report from K Maheshwari  
‘Although I am unable to attend this meeting, I would like to provide a brief update. 
I continue to hold regular meetings with constituents and remain accessible by email and 
through my social media channels, ensuring residents can contact me whenever they need 
assistance. 
Where issues raised by residents require the involvement of Ramsey Town Council, I copy 
the Town Council into the relevant correspondence so that matters can be dealt with 
collaboratively. 
Since the last Town Council meeting, no issues have been referred to me by Ramsey Town 
Council that require an update. However, I remain available to assist the Town Council, 
fellow councillors and residents whenever support is needed. Please do not hesitate to 
contact me if there are any district council matters on which I can help. 
Thank you, and I look forward to continuing to work together for the benefit of Ramsey and 
the surrounding communities. 
Thanks 
Kind regards 
Cllr Karan Maheshwari 
Council members were very disappointed that there was no District Councillor present to 
represent Huntingdonshire District Council and asked the Clerk to raise this with them. 
Further feedback was that in Cllr Maheshwari report he stated he had not been asked to do 
any work on behalf of Ramsey Town Council, Cllr S Corney reminded members that he been 
asked to speak to Huntingdonshire District Council about the land at the back of the Doctors 
Surgery on Mews Close, and that Cllr S Corney had spoken to him at length after the 
meeting about the project and how to approach the Officers. It was also commented that Cllr 

2 
 
K Maheshwari had been promoting all local events and had not promoted the 4
th
 July Party 
in the Park a Town Council event. The Clerk had been asked to correspond with the three 
District Councillors for clarity on these issues and to gain commitment for future meetings. 
 
259. Planning Applications for Consideration 
1.1  26/01152/OUT Proposed  outline  application  for  development  of  up  to  19  residential 
dwellings  with  matters  committed  to  access.  Hankins  Garage  46  Whytefield  Road.  Ramsey 
PE26 1AH.After a lengthy discussion Proposed by Cllr L Webster and seconded by Cllr S Fice 
Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for the District Council to APPROVE the outline 
plan but wanted the following comments to be noted for further plans.  
Ramsey Town Council members suggested the following: 
• having a lesser number of houses on the plot and increase the number of car parking 
spaces.  
• To have allocated visitor parking to take pressure away from Whytefield Road.  
• Have concerns where the flow of the attenuation pond would flow to 
• Suggest bungalow housing maybe preferable and take pressure away from parking 
spaces required. 
• There is a strip of land that goes from the site to Blenheim Road and even though it is 
outside of the application boundary was assurance this would not be used for traffic. 
• Council felt the application should make S106 and CIL contribution. 
260. Planning Other Business 
a) TRO – pedestrianisation – The Clerk informed members that the TRO was now being looked 
at by Cambridgeshire Highways and work should start in September. 
b) Street Naming to be noted. Static Caravan, Land Southeast of True Briton, Middle Drove, 
Ramsey Heights to be known as Hare’s Place - Noted 
c) Cllr V Fendley informed members that Huntingdonshire District Council had appointed the 
Independent Assessor for the Ramsey Communities Neighbourhood Plan and they had 
started to ask questions which Anthony Northcote the Planning Advisor was answering. Cllr J 
Clarke asked if the answers would go through Ramsey Town Council, Cllr V Fendley 
reminded Members that the Ramsey Communities Neighbourhood Plan Steering Group 
would be overseeing the process. 
 
261. Finance Items. 
a) Financial Summary – Cashbook to 30/06/2026 which was tabled. Noted. 
b) Expenditure Transactions to be approved. Proposed by Cllr S Corney and seconded by 
Cllr A Austin Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for the expenditure transactions 
to be APPROVED 
c) The Clerk informed Members that the invoice had been received from Ramsey 
Neighbourhoods Trust for £3750. Cllr I Axelsen declared a non-pecuniary interest in this item 
as Chair of Ramsey Neighbourhoods Trust and would not vote. After a discussion on how the 
youth provision was improving it was Proposed by Cllr S Fice and seconded by Cllr M Clarke 
Ramsey Town Council voted 10 FOR and 1 ABSTENTION for the Clerk to pay the invoice. 
 
262. Working Party Recommendations. 
Cemetery Working Party 
For Council to agree to explore the option of having green burials in the Cemetery 
Extension, working in partnership with Muchwood. Cllr M Clarke informed members of the 
discussion that had taken place with herself, Cllr A Costello, Chris from Muchwood and the 
Clerk. The recommendation was for the Cemetery Working Party to look further into 
partnership working with Muchwood for a Green Burial Site on the extension section of the 
Wood Lane Cemetery. Proposed by Cllr M Clarke and seconded by Cllr A Costello, Ramsey 

3 
 
Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for the Cemetery Working Party to continue to explore 
the opportunity for partnership working and feed back to Full Council. 
Cllr M Clarke handed over to Cllr A Costello for an update on the Mortuary Chapel. 
Cllr A Costello informed members that she had met with Nick Armour from Huntingdonshire 
District Council Conservation Team. The most urgent part of the restoration was to remove 
the glass of the contagion windows. Cllr A Costello had been contacting glass companies 
but there was a resistance to do the work. Cllr S Corney had passed on a contact who is 
prepared to do the work and is a Carpenter and Glazier, within the previously agreed limit 
and using the money donated by the Friends of the Mortuary Chapel the Clerk had engaged 
Sean Bellamy at a cost of £600 to remove the glass. 
Nick Armour also said to Councillor A Costello that with the plans the Town Council had for 
the site we should explore using Huntingdonshire District Council CIL funds. 
 
263. Abuse towards Council Employees and Ramsey Town Councillors. 
Ramsey Town Council Members had been made aware of a known individual who had been 
targeting the Town Clerk with verbal abuse, this person had also been abusive toward other 
Councillors and members of the public. This is now being investigated by Cambridgeshire 
Police. Cllr A Austin reminded the Clerk that if she requires immediate support to call the 
Emergency What’s App and a member would come to support. The Clerk along with council 
staff have access to a panic button as part of the Lone Working Policy. It was agreed the 
situation would be monitored. 
 
264. TOWN MAYOR’S AND CLERK’S CORRESPONDENCE: 
a) Cllr H Tobias email to the Clerk and response – Council to consider if any further 
comments are required – letter previously circulated. The Clerk had previously circulated an 
email and response that she had received from Huntingdonshire District Councillor for 
Ramsey Cllr Howard Tobias. The Clerk was instructed to write a further letter to Cllr H 
Tobais explaining the legislation that Town Council follow and cannot raise funds for other 
public bodies, to advise Cllr H Tobias to have a meeting with the Police and Crime 
Commissioner Daryl Preston who can influence where funds are spent on Policing. The 
Clerk was also asked to reiterate that the offer to use the facilities of Ramsey Town Council, 
the library was still available and to explore the use of the Ramsey Fire Station. 
 
b) Parking on Abbey Road. The Clerk informed Council that residents of Abbey Road had 
expressed concern over the parking plans at Abbey College. They were currently suffering 
from excess parking outside their properties and wanted to know what they could do. The 
Clerk had spoken with them and given advice. Cllr J Clarke did not think the road was 
private as the council had adopted the road from Hollow Lane to the Last house. Cllr J 
Bufton thought the bus turn around and the road to the school could be private and belong to 
the school. Cllr J Bufton suggested we note the residents’ comments but knowing that there 
will always have parking in Abbey Road because the school shut the gates for a short period 
of time each day.  
 
265. Freedom of Information Request from Ramsey Town Council 
FOI received from Huntingdonshire District Council this had previously been circulated to 
members and whilst they were disappointed in the response no further action would take 
place at this time. 
FOI Cambridgeshire Police – a response had now been received and would be circulated to 
members. 
 
266. ATTENDANCES AT MEETINGS AND ORGANISATIONS: 
• Cllr V Fendley and Cllr R Terrill had attended the Bishop of Ely’s Garden Party, a 
lovely event and was able to meet many other dignitaries from Cambridgeshire. 

4 
 
• The Clerk fed back from the 4
th
 July event, saying the feedback was, more please, 
and that ideas had been given for future event. 
• Cllr V Fendley fed back on a meeting she had attended online with Michelle Sacks 
CEO of Huntingdonshire District Council. Elections for the shadow authorities will 
take place next May. There is not an appeal process but if the authority had a strong 
case it could go to judicial review, or they could ask for some boundary amendments. 
The transition will still happen in May 2028. Regarding selling of Community Assets, 
they must still follow process and not sell the assets cheaply as it could impact the 
new Unitary. CIL can still be awarded even if it is for a future project and the funds 
can be ring-fenced. 
• Cllr C Maskell fed back about how well the Bands on the Green had been, each 
week had seen more than one hundred plus residents of all ages. 
• Cllr S Fice had attended the Ramsey St Mary’s PCC Strawberry Tea, which helps 
raise funds towards keeping the church open. 
• Cllr V Fendley informed members that the Project team had appointed Retail Revival 
to put together two business plans; one would be if Council was operating and one if 
it was operated through a social enterprise. 
•  Cllr V Fendley and the Clerk attended the Ramsey Junior School Eco Day and gave 
away previously prepared envelopes of wildflower seed by the Council staff team for 
the children to spread in their gardens. 
• Cllr V Fendley thanked the Council for supporting Once Upon a Time in Fenland 
which took place at Ramsey Rural Museum. Children from Ramsey Junior school 
and Ashbeach school attended and with the extra showing funded by Ramsey Town 
Council other groups including the Brownies attended meaning over 200 children had 
seen the show. 
           Cllr C Maskell left the meeting at 8:20pm 
 
• Cllr V Fendley had also attended the Ramsey Rotary handover and informed 
members that Chris Wick would be the President for this year. 
• Cllr V Fendley attended the Army Cadet showcase in Waterbeach, supporting the 
Ramsey Cadets and was disappointed no other Mayor’s supported their groups. 
• Cllr V Fendley attended AGE UK launch of Befriending Service in care homes. 60% 
of people in care homes do not receive visitors. This was held at Magnolia Park. 
• Cllr R Terrill and Cllr V Fendley attended the online Police meeting with Inspector 
Colin Norden. When challenged about the lack of PCSO’s for Ramsey they were 
informed there were two for Ramsey unfortunately they do not have the transport to 
get from St Ives to Ramsey. Cllr J Clarke commented that there are always vehicles 
at the Huntingdon Police Station perhaps they could use them. Cllr R Terrill had 
suggested they use their own transport to get here and claim mileage. Cllr R Terrill 
was asked to follow this matter and report back to members. 
267. Meeting Dates 
The next meeting of Ramsey Town Council would take place on Thursday 23rd July 7pm 
(Planning). 
 
 
Town Mayor_______________________________________Date___________________

• Cllr V Fendley had also attended the Ramsey Rotary handover and informed members that Chris Wick would be the President for this year. • Cllr V Fendley attended the Army Cadet showcase in Waterbeach, supporting the Ramsey Cadets and was disappointed no other Mayor’s supported their groups. • Cllr V Fendley attended AGE UK launch of Befriending Service in care homes. 60% of people in care homes do not receive visitors. This was held at Magnolia Park. • Cllr R Terrill and Cllr V Fendley attended the online Police meeting with Inspector Colin Norden. When challenged about the lack of PCSO’s for Ramsey they were informed there were two for Ramsey unfortunately they do not have the transport to get from St Ives to Ramsey. Cllr J Clarke commented that there are always vehicles at the Huntingdon Police Station perhaps they could use them. Cllr R Terrill had suggested they use their own transport to get here and claim mileage. Cllr R Terrill was asked to follow this matter and report back to members. 267. Meeting Dates The next meeting of Ramsey Town Council would take place on Thursday 23rd July 7pm (Planning).

You are hereby summoned to attend a meeting of Ramsey Town Council to be held in The Lavender Room, 
Ramsey Town Council Great Whyte, Ramsey on Thursday 27 August 2026 at 7.00pm, when the following 
items of business will be transacted: - 
 
 
Please ensure all mobile phones are switched off or turned to silent during the meeting. 
 
A G E N D A  
   APOLOGIES FOR ABSENCE 
 
1. DECLARATIONS OF INTEREST 
To receive declarations from Members as to disclosable pecuniary and other interests and the nature of 
those interests in relation to any agenda item. 
   
2. PUBLIC PARTICIPATION 
To allow 20 minutes for any members of the public to address the Council.  
 
3. MINUTES 
To approve as a correct record, the Minutes of the meeting of the Council held on 13th August 2026 – 
attached. 
 
4. PLANNING 
1.1 26/01416/HHFUL – Erection of two storey extension, barn and carport, internal and external 
alterations, new dormer and canopy roofs and installation of solar PV panels. – Heathfield, Benwick 
Road, Ramsey Forty Foot, Huntingdon. 
1.2 26/01206/OUT- Proposed demolition of an existing dwelling and outbuilding and replacement with 4 
new dwellings (outline application with all matters reserved, with the exception of access) – 190 
Herne Road, Ramsey St Marys.

St Marys. 
 
5. CONSULTATION ON THE REVIEWED BURY DRAFT NEIGHBOURHOOD PLAN 
Ramsey Town Council comments to be agreed.

Would Cllrs please make time to look at the planning items on the District Council’s website 
before the meeting by accessing the HDC planning portal.

The next meeting of Ramsey Town Council will take place at 7pm on 10th September 2026.

MINUTES OF RAMSEY TOWN COUNCIL MEETING 
held at 7pm on Thursday 13 August 2026 at  
Ramsey Town Council Great Whyte, Ramsey 
 
 
Present:  Councillors: I Axelsen, J Clarke, M Clarke, S Corney (Dep Mayor), A Costello, V Fendley (Mayor), L Knight, C 
Maskell, R Terrill, L Webster, and E Welsh. 
In attendance: Mrs L Renfree, Town Clerk  
274. Apologies for Absence. 
Cllrs J Aubin, A Austin, J Bufton, S Fice, and P Rose. 
 
275.To Receive Declarations of Interest. 
No declarations of interest were received. 
 
276. Public Participation. 
There were 10 members of the public present. 
 
277. Minutes of the Last Meeting to be Approved. 
To  approve  as  a  correct  record,  the  minutes  of  the  meeting  Council  held  on  23rd  July  2026,  previously circulated. 
Proposed  by  Cllr  S  Corney  and  seconded  by  Cllr  R  Terrill  Ramsey  Town  Council  voted UNANIMOUSLY to  accept  the 
minutes of 23rd July as a true record. 
 
278. Co-option of New Town Councillor. 
Three  candidates  put  themselves  forward  for  co-option,  each  applicant  addressed  the  members  giving  an  overview  of 
themselves  and  why  they  felt  they  would  be  a  good  addition  to  the  Town  Council.  The  members  voted  and  Jessie 
Thompson received the most votes and would join the council at their August planning meeting. 
 
279. District and County Councillor Update: 
Cllrs Coogan, Maheshwari and Tobias were invited to update members of District and County Council matters, apologies 
received  from  Cllr  R  Coogan,  and  a  report tabled to  members. No  apologies  from  Cllr  Maheshwari.  Cllr  Tobias  reported 
back in person at the meeting as follows: Cllr Tobias informed members that he does not use social media to conduct his 
council  business  both  at  District  and  County  level  and  is  looking  to  work  in  collaboration  with  the  council and  residents, 
listening  and  challenging  to  make  the  Ramsey  ward  a  better  place  to  be.  Since  the  Huntingdonshire  District  Council 
meeting Cllr Tobias had been looking into the parking assessment and challenging the fact there is no business case for 
spending £370,000 of taxpayer’s money. Cllr Tobias informed members that some Ramsey plans were being discussed at 
the next Development Management Committee meeting. Cllr Tobias was happy to support CIL (Community Infrastructure 
Levy) applications if they will support the wider community. From a County Council perspective Cllr Tobias had been in the 
role  for  28  days  and  had  planned  to  meet  Highways  looking  at  the  road  infrastructure  and  is  looking  at  the  Student  Bus 
situation  where  the  decision  was  made  by  the  Peterborough  College.  The  Clerk  was  asked  to  communicate  with  Cllr 
Tobias to continue the work asked of Cllr Maheshwari on securing the land for the car park on Mews Close. 
 
 
 
280. Planning Applications for Consideration 
1.1 26/01128/LBC – Injection  of  a  SecoMUR  chemical  damp  proof  course  into  drilled  holes  to  all  external  walls  and  solid 
brick internal walls- Bridge Farm 15 Ramsey Road, Ramsey Forty Foot. Proposed by Cllr S Corney and seconded by Cllr M 
Clarke Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for Huntingdonshire District Council to APPROVE the application. 
1.2 26/01328/HHFUL – Replacement of damaged cladding to front, side and rear of the property- 17 Wyatt Close, Ramsey. 
Proposed by Cllr S Corney and seconded by L Webster Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for Huntingdonshire 
District Council to APPROVE the application, there was neighbouring support for the application, and  it is  in keeping  with 
the area. 
1.3 26/01385/FUL- Change of use of land from agricultural to residential curtilage associated with Kingfisher House – 
Kingfisher House, Whittlesey Road, Benwick, March. Proposed by Cllr C Maskell and seconded by Cllr J Clarke Ramsey 
Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for Huntingdonshire District Council to APPROVE the application. 
1.4 26/01352/FUL – Change of use of land to a gypsy and traveller residential pitch comprising the siting of one 
mobile home, one amenity building, associated hardstanding and ancillary works (part retrospective). – 
Land East of Fern Cottage, Harpers Drove, Ramsey Heights. The Clerk had received objections to the 
application from residents of Ramsey Heights as previously agreed with Huntingdonshire District Council. 
The Clerk was asked to submit to the planning portal their objections as laid out in the 21-page report 
previously circulated. Cllr A Costello proposed REFUSAL and Cllr seconded by Cllr L Webster Ramsey 
Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for the District Council to REFUSE this application. The Clerk would 
also put the residents’ comments to the planning portal. 
 

281. Planning Other Business: 
a) Pedestrianisation update: Cllr V Fendley informed members that the TRO was live and that there would 
be a planning application being submitted for the shop in a box units. 
b) Abbey College LHI BID- The plans were out for consultation and Ramsey Town Council were asked if 
they wanted to add any further comments on the plan. Ramsey Town Council did not want to add any 
further comments. 
c) Consultation on the Reviewed Bury Village Draft Neighbourhood Plan – Cllr V Fendley talked through the 
Goals and Objectives from the Bury Village Neighbourhood Plan and informed members it would be on 
the agenda for the next planning meeting for comment. 
d) To note the Tree Preservation Order26/002 – Ramsey Rural Museum had been confirmed. Noted 
e) Notice of application for a Town/ Village Green, Abbey Green, Ramsey. Noted. 
f) Huntingdonshire District Council Local Plan Consultation – Members to agree to using Anthony Northcote 
for advice regarding Ramsey Town Council’s response. Proposed by Cllr L Knight and seconded by Cllr R 
Terrill Ramsey town Council voted 10 FOR and 1 AGAINST for the Clerk to instruct Anthony Northcote to 
give advice to Ramsey Town Council to comment on Huntingdonshire District Council’s Local Plan. 
282. Finance Items: 
a) Financial Summary – Cash book to 31/07/2026 tabled – Noted 
b) Expenditure Transactions to be approved – tabled- Proposed by Cllr S Corney and seconded by Cllr L 
Knight Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY to agree the expenditure transactions. 
283. Working Part Recommendations: 
 Recommendations from the Economic Development Working Party 
a) For Ramsey Town Council to agree in principle to take control of the shop in a box units moving forward 
post successful TRO and Full Planning approval, and for Ramsey Town Council to manage the gated 
timings – Proposed by Cllr L Knight and seconded by Cllr S Corney Ramsey Town Council voted 10 FOR 
and 1 ABSTENTION for Ramsey Town Council to in principle take control of the Shop in a box units 
subject to a successful TRO and Full Planning approval. Proposed by Cllr L Knight and seconded by Cllr 
S Corney Ramsey Town Council voted 10 FOR and 1 ABSTENTION for Ramsey Town Council to 
manage the gated timings. 
b) For Ramsey Town Council to initiate a Local Business Group to engage with our local businesses, with a 
view to sharing information. It was felt that a communication streamline to all Ramsey Parish Businesses 
was lacking and that this meeting would bring them together to explore a process moving forward. 
Proposed by Cllr L Knight and seconded by Cllr S Corney Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY 
for a business meeting to be arranged in September. 
Recommendations from the Amenities, Highways, Health, and Leisure Working Party. 
a) For Ramsey Town Council to decide between two quotes for the Public Toilet Doors both quotes ex vat. 
The quote covers three new doors: Healthmatic £8040 or LAM Automation Ltd £8660 – The Clerk made 
an amendment to the cost of the Healthmatic quote £10,050. Proposed by Cllr A Costello and seconded 
by Cllr C Maskell Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY to accept the quote from LAM 
Automation LTD at a cost of £8,660.00 and the funds would come from the CIL account.  
b) For Ramsey Town Council to decide if they want the public toilet doors to have windows in them at a cost 
of £700 ex vat. Proposed by Cllr J Clarke and seconded by Cllr C Maskell to REFUSE the windows in the 
public toilet doors. Ramsey Town Council voted REFUSE 6 and 3 AGAINST 2 ABSTENTIONS for the 
public toilets to not have windows. 
c) For Ramsey Town Council to agree in principle a large mural sited at the QEII Skatepark. Final design to 
be voted on in the future. - paper circulated. After a long discussion on the subject, it was agreed 
UNANIMOUSLY for the proposal to go back to Amenities, Highways, Health & Leisure for further 
exploration. 
Recommendations from the Communications Working Party. 
      a) To Agree the draft Digital Screen Policy for Ramsey Town Council previously                                                                                       
circulated. Proposed by Cllr L Knight and seconded by Cllr S Corney Ramsey Town Council voted 10 FOR and 1 
ABSTENTION to APPROVE the Digital Screen Policy. 
a) To Agree the Risk Assessment for Public Meetings at Ramsey Town Council- previously 
circulated. Proposed by Cllr L Knight and seconded by Cllr S Corney. Ramsey Town Council 
voted 9 FOR and 2 ABSTENTIONS to APPROVE the Risk Assessment for Public Meetings. 
b) To Agree the Risk Assessment for Premises and Buildings- previously circulated. Proposed by 
Cllr L Knight and seconded by Cllr S Corney Ramsey Town Council vote 9 FOR and 2 
ABSTENTIONS to APPROVE the Risk Assessment for Premises and Buildings. 

c) To Review the current IT Policy – previously circulated. Proposed by Cllr L Knight and seconded 
by Cllr S Corney Ramsey Town Council voted 10 FOR and 1 ABSTENTION to APPROVE the 
updated IT Policy. 
d) To agree the new email footer –tabled. Proposed by Cllr L Knight and seconded by Cllr S Corney 
Ramsey Town Council vote 10 FOR and 1 ABSTENTION to use the footer tabled for Councillor 
emails. The Clerk will circulate to members to use. 
284. WORKING PARTY UPDATE  
a) Members to receive an update from the Chair of each Working Party- previously circulated. Cllr L 
Knight said this was a very useful document and is a really good idea. The document was noted. 
 
285. FEEDBACK FROM GRANT FROM COMMUNITY SAFETY & SAFETY PARTNERSHIP. 
a) Feedback from Future Scooter Foundation -the Clerk showed two small video clips from some of 
the young people who participated in the evening event. There was a positive debate, and it was 
agreed that it would be good to have more young girls participating. Noted 
 
286. TOWN MAYOR’S AND CLERK’S CORRESPONDENCE: 
a) Update on Anti-Social Behaviour on the Clerk and Council. The Clerk updated members on the 
investigation with Huntingdonshire District Council Anti-Social behaviour team. They are now 
looking to produce a Criminal Behaviour Order to protect the Council. 
b) Resident communication on noise from skate park and concerns RTC would put lighting there for 
after dark use. The Clerk informed members that a resident after reading a District Councillors 
post on having lighting at the Skatepark was very upset as Ramsey Town Council had said that 
would not be the case. Cllr Fendley was very clear that there would be no plans to light up the 
Skatepark. 
c) Resident communication on thanking the Town Council for the work Paul and Morgan are doing 
keeping the Cemetery clear and improving the area. The Clerk informed members that positive 
comments had been received about the work in clearing the Cemetery. 
d) Thank you from the Ramsey Garden and Horticulture Club for the grant we gave them which 
enable two new competitions this year. Cllr Fendley informed members of the letter received 
thanking Ramsey Town Council for their grant and the opportunities it has given their club. 
e) Ramsey Heights residents concern over lack of Fire Hydrant for the Droves. After the fire on 
Harpers Drove, residents were concerned that the Fire Service had to keep going away to refill 
the tanker. This was noted. 
Councillor Costello left the meeting at 8:55pm. 
287. ATTENDANCES AT MEETINGS AND ORGANISATIONS: 
a) Safer Communities Public Meeting - Cllr V Fendley fed back on the public meeting held at 
Ramsey Forty Foot. Cllr V Fendley praised the Inspector for his honesty during the meeting, but 
the overall outcome was we do live in a safe community. 
b) Mayor met with County Councillor Cllr H Tobias. Cllr V Fendley informed members that she had 
had a meeting and discussed the LHI bids and infrastructure. 
c) Magnolia Park Opening Day- Cllr V Fendley attended the opening and it was a very positive day. 
d) Jones Court 40
th
 Anniversary BBQ – Cllr V Fendley and the Clerk attended the BBQ, and Cllr V 
Fendley had the difficult task of judging the baking competition. 
e) Update on correspondence with Cambridgeshire Constabulary – Cllr R Terrill updated members 
on his conversation with Inspector Norden. 
f) MP Sam Carling – Local Surgery Date 14
th
 August 2026. Cllr V Fendley informed members that 
the MP was in the community meeting with residents. 
 
288. MEETING DATES 
The next meeting of Ramsey Town Council (Planning) will take place on 27th August 2026 at 7pm.  
 
 
Town Mayor_______________________________________Date___________________

Cllr A Costello proposed REFUSAL and Cllr seconded by Cllr L Webster Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for the District Council to REFUSE this application. The Clerk would also put the residents’ comments to the planning portal.

281. Planning Other Business: a) Pedestrianisation update: Cllr V Fendley informed members that the TRO was live and that there would be a planning application being submitted for the shop in a box units. b) Abbey College LHI BID- The plans were out for consultation and Ramsey Town Council were asked if they wanted to add any further comments on the plan. Ramsey Town Council did not want to add any further comments. c) Consultation on the Reviewed Bury Village Draft Neighbourhood Plan – Cllr V Fendley talked through the Goals and Objectives from the Bury Village Neighbourhood Plan and informed members it would be on the agenda for the next planning meeting for comment. d) To note the Tree Preservation Order26/002 – Ramsey Rural Museum had been confirmed. Noted e) Notice of application for a Town/ Village Green, Abbey Green, Ramsey. Noted. f) Huntingdonshire District Council Local Plan Consultation – Members to agree to using Anthony Northcote for advice regarding Ramsey Town Council’s response. Proposed by Cllr L Knight and seconded by Cllr R Terrill Ramsey town Council voted 10 FOR and 1 AGAINST for the Clerk to instruct Anthony Northcote to give advice to Ramsey Town Council to comment on Huntingdonshire District Council’s Local Plan. 282. Finance Items: a) Financial Summary – Cash book to 31/07/2026 tabled – Noted b) Expenditure Transactions to be approved – tabled- Proposed by Cllr S Corney and seconded by Cllr L Knight Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY to agree the expenditure transactions. 283. Working Part Recommendations: Recommendations from the Economic Development Working Party a) For Ramsey Town Council to agree in principle to take control of the shop in a box units moving forward post successful TRO and Full Planning approval, and for Ramsey Town Council to manage the gated timings – Proposed by Cllr L Knight and seconded by Cllr S Corney Ramsey Town Council voted 10 FOR and 1 ABSTENTION for Ramsey Town Council to in principle take control of the Shop in a box units subject to a successful TRO and Full Planning approval. Proposed by Cllr L Knight and seconded by Cllr S Corney Ramsey Town Council voted 10 FOR and 1 ABSTENTION for Ramsey Town Council to manage the gated timings. b) For Ramsey Town Council to initiate a Local Business Group to engage with our local businesses, with a view to sharing information. It was felt that a communication streamline to all Ramsey Parish Businesses was lacking and that this meeting would bring them together to explore a process moving forward. Proposed by Cllr L Knight and seconded by Cllr S Corney Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for a business meeting to be arranged in September. Recommendations from the Amenities, Highways, Health, and Leisure Working Party. a) For Ramsey Town Council to decide between two quotes for the Public Toilet Doors both quotes ex vat. The quote covers three new doors: Healthmatic £8040 or LAM Automation Ltd £8660 – The Clerk made an amendment to the cost of the Healthmatic quote £10,050. Proposed by Cllr A Costello and seconded by Cllr C Maskell Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY to accept the quote from LAM Automation LTD at a cost of £8,660.00 and the funds would come from the CIL account. b) For Ramsey Town Council to decide if they want the public toilet doors to have windows in them at a cost of £700 ex vat. Proposed by Cllr J Clarke and seconded by Cllr C Maskell to REFUSE the windows in the public toilet doors. Ramsey Town Council voted REFUSE 6 and 3 AGAINST 2 ABSTENTIONS for the public toilets to not have windows. c) For Ramsey Town Council to agree in principle a large mural sited at the QEII Skatepark. Final design to be voted on in the future. - paper circulated. After a long discussion on the subject, it was agreed UNANIMOUSLY for the proposal to go back to Amenities, Highways, Health & Leisure for further exploration. Recommendations from the Communications Working Party. a) To Agree the draft Digital Screen Policy for Ramsey Town Council previously circulated. Proposed by Cllr L Knight and seconded by Cllr S Corney Ramsey Town Council voted 10 FOR and 1 ABSTENTION to APPROVE the Digital Screen Policy. a) To Agree the Risk Assessment for Public Meetings at Ramsey Town Council- previously circulated. Proposed by Cllr L Knight and seconded by Cllr S Corney. Ramsey Town Council voted 9 FOR and 2 ABSTENTIONS to APPROVE the Risk Assessment for Public Meetings. b) To Agree the Risk Assessment for Premises and Buildings- previously circulated. Proposed by Cllr L Knight and seconded by Cllr S Corney Ramsey Town Council vote 9 FOR and 2 ABSTENTIONS to APPROVE the Risk Assessment for Premises and Buildings.

c) To Review the current IT Policy – previously circulated. Proposed by Cllr L Knight and seconded by Cllr S Corney Ramsey Town Council voted 10 FOR and 1 ABSTENTION to APPROVE the updated IT Policy. d) To agree the new email footer –tabled. Proposed by Cllr L Knight and seconded by Cllr S Corney Ramsey Town Council vote 10 FOR and 1 ABSTENTION to use the footer tabled for Councillor emails. The Clerk will circulate to members to use. 284. WORKING PARTY UPDATE a) Members to receive an update from the Chair of each Working Party- previously circulated. Cllr L Knight said this was a very useful document and is a really good idea. The document was noted.

285. FEEDBACK FROM GRANT FROM COMMUNITY SAFETY & SAFETY PARTNERSHIP. a) Feedback from Future Scooter Foundation -the Clerk showed two small video clips from some of the young people who participated in the evening event. There was a positive debate, and it was agreed that it would be good to have more young girls participating. Noted

286. TOWN MAYOR’S AND CLERK’S CORRESPONDENCE: a) Update on Anti-Social Behaviour on the Clerk and Council. The Clerk updated members on the investigation with Huntingdonshire District Council Anti-Social behaviour team. They are now looking to produce a Criminal Behaviour Order to protect the Council. b) Resident communication on noise from skate park and concerns RTC would put lighting there for after dark use. The Clerk informed members that a resident after reading a District Councillors post on having lighting at the Skatepark was very upset as Ramsey Town Council had said that would not be the case. Cllr Fendley was very clear that there would be no plans to light up the Skatepark. c) Resident communication on thanking the Town Council for the work Paul and Morgan are doing keeping the Cemetery clear and improving the area. The Clerk informed members that positive comments had been received about the work in clearing the Cemetery. d) Thank you from the Ramsey Garden and Horticulture Club for the grant we gave them which enable two new competitions this year. Cllr Fendley informed members of the letter received thanking Ramsey Town Council for their grant and the opportunities it has given their club. e) Ramsey Heights residents concern over lack of Fire Hydrant for the Droves. After the fire on Harpers Drove, residents were concerned that the Fire Service had to keep going away to refill the tanker. This was noted. Councillor Costello left the meeting at 8:55pm. 287. ATTENDANCES AT MEETINGS AND ORGANISATIONS: a) Safer Communities Public Meeting - Cllr V Fendley fed back on the public meeting held at Ramsey Forty Foot. Cllr V Fendley praised the Inspector for his honesty during the meeting, but the overall outcome was we do live in a safe community. b) Mayor met with County Councillor Cllr H Tobias. Cllr V Fendley informed members that she had had a meeting and discussed the LHI bids and infrastructure. c) Magnolia Park Opening Day- Cllr V Fendley attended the opening and it was a very positive day. d) Jones Court 40 th Anniversary BBQ – Cllr V Fendley and the Clerk attended the BBQ, and Cllr V Fendley had the difficult task of judging the baking competition. e) Update on correspondence with Cambridgeshire Constabulary – Cllr R Terrill updated members on his conversation with Inspector Norden. f) MP Sam Carling – Local Surgery Date 14 th August 2026. Cllr V Fendley informed members that the MP was in the community meeting with residents.
288. MEETING DATES The next meeting of Ramsey Town Council (Planning) will take place on 27th August 2026 at 7pm.

MINUTES OF RAMSEY TOWN COUNCIL MEETING 
held at 7pm on Thursday 24 September 2026 at  
Ramsey Town Council Great Whyte, Ramsey 
 
 
Present:    Councillors: A Austin, I Axelsen, J Clarke, M Clarke, V Fendley (Mayor), S Fice, 
L Knight, P Rose, R Terrill, J Thompson, and L Webster. 
In attendance: Mrs L Renfree, Town Clerk  
 
312. Apologies for Absence. 
Cllrs J Bufton, S Corney (representing the Council at RAF Wyton) A Costello, C Maskell, and 
E Welsh. 
 
313.To Receive Declarations of Interest. 
No declarations of interest were made. 
 
314. Public Participation. 
There was one member of the public who wished to thank the Town Council for awarding her 
the Freedom of the Town. 
 
315. Minutes of the Last Meeting to be Approved. 
Proposed by Cllr A Austin and seconded by Cllr R Terrill, Councillors voted unanimously to 
accept the Minutes of the meeting of the Council held on 10
th
 September 2026 as a correct 
record. 
 
316. Planning Applications for Consideration. 
1.1 25/01382/OUT Outline application with all matters reserved save for access for erection 
of up to 199 dwellings including open space, play space, car parking, drainage, utilities 
connections and the construction of a new access off Stoneman Way and Biggin Lane – 
further information received. Proposed by Cllr S Fice and seconded by Cllr P Rose Ramsey 
Town Council members voted UNANIMOUSLY for the District Council to REFUSE the 
application. The traffic assessment had not been actioned on the correct miles per hour- it 
stated 30mph when it is 20mph road. It is in Bury Parish Council’s adopted Local Plan and in 
the Draft Local Plan for Ramsey that the land needs to remain undeveloped to stop further 
coalescence between Bury Village and Ramsey Town. Drainage remains a concern for 
members for the area of land not having enough drainage in place and water would then be 
flowing into Slade Dyke. 
 
1.2 26/00681/FUL Construction of 2 drive-thru units (sui generis) with associated hard and 
soft landscaping – Plot 09A St Marys Road, Ramsey. Proposed by Cllr P Rose and seconded 
by Cllr S Fice Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for the District Council to 
APPROVE the application.  
 
1.3 26/01584/FUL Open storage of vehicles (Use Class B8) in association with the adjacent 
vehicle scrapping, recycling, and export businesses – Land South of The Foundry, Factory 
Bank, Ramsey. Proposed by Cllr L Knight and seconded by Cllr R Terrill Ramsey Town 
Council voted 11 FOR and 1 ABSTENTION for the Clerk to gain further information before a 
formal vote would be submitted. The questions to be asked were, has the land had change of 
use from agricultural land? Has the environmental work been looked at for contamination? 
Has the drainage been looked at? Concerns on the land encroaching the area that would be 
siting the MUGA on the Northern Gateway. 
 
 

2 
 
1.4 26/01670/S73 Variation of condition 2 (Approved Plans – Planning Applications) of 
25/02222/FUL – Land Rear of 192 Oilmills Road, Ramsey Mereside. Proposed by Cllr S 
Fice and seconded by Cllr M Clarke Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for the 
District Council to APPROVE the application. Council saw no reason to object to the 
variations being made 
317. Planning – other business 
a) Somersham Neighbourhood Plan Consultation Ramsey Town Council comments 
to be agreed. Ramsey Town Council comments were to wish them well with their 
Local Plan. 
b) Street Naming: Equestrian Facilities, Land on south side of Middle Drove, Ramsey 
Heights to be known as The Meadows, Middle Drove, Ramsey Heights. Noted 
 
c) Huntingdonshire Pre Submission Local Plan – 2046, Ramsey Town Council 
response – Email received regarding Site Allocation Bury 1 (Old Station Road, Bury 
development) – previously circulated. Proposed by Cllr S Fice and seconded by Cllr A 
Austin the members voted UNANIMOUSLY for the Clerk to forward the email to the 
Planning consultant to add into their response. 
 
d) Mews Car Park and Great Whyte Improvements Update – The Mayor Cllr V 
Fendley updated the members on the two meetings she had had with the Portfolio 
holder for Governance about the Pedestrianisation Project. They felt it was a positive 
project and could see the benefits it would bring to the town. The Portfolio Holder also 
felt the land at the back of the Doctors on Mews Close was required for parking and 
asked the District Council team to move forward with the agreement of a Town 
Council lease hold of 50 years. He encouraged the Mayor to apply for this round of 
the HDC CIL funding to enable the work. 
 
318. Residents Communication. 
a) Draft newsletter – Cllr A Austin tabled the newsletter which was authorised to go to 
print. 
 
319. Meeting Dates 
The next meeting of Ramsey Town Council would take place on Thursday 8th October at 
7pm. 
 
 
Town Mayor_______________________________________Date___________________

1 
 
 
MINUTES OF RAMSEY TOWN COUNCIL MEETING 
held at 7pm on Thursday 08 October 2026 at  
Ramsey Town Council Great Whyte, Ramsey 
 
 
Present:    Councillors: A Austin, I Axelsen, J Bufton, J Clarke, M Clarke, Cllrs S Corney, V 
Fendley (Mayor), S Fice, L Knight, P Rose, R Terrill, J Thompson, L Webster and E Welsh. 
In attendance: Mrs L Renfree, Town Clerk  
 
320. Apologies for Absence. 
 Cllrs A Costello, C Maskell. 
 
321.To Receive Declarations of Interest. 
No declarations of interest were made at that point. 
 
322. Public Participation. 
There was six members of  the  public  who discussed  planning  1.3, discussing the potential 
199 David  Wilson  Homes  which was  going  to  be  debated  on  19
th
 October  at  Development 
Management Panel and a question was raised to be answered post that meeting on where 
the community would stand to make a legal challenge. 
 
323. Minutes of the Last Meeting to be Approved. 
Proposed by Cllr S Corney and seconded by Cllr L Knight, Councillors voted 13 FOR and 2 
ABSTENSIONS for the Minutes of the meeting of the Council held on 24
th
 September 2026 
as a correct record. 
 
324.County and District Councillor Update. 
County and District Councillor Cllr H Tobias attended the meeting to feedback on both County 
and District matters. Cllr Tobias outlined two visits to Ashbeach School and Abbey College 
and  commented  on  the  challenges  that  Ashbeach  faced  with  lack  of  SEN  funding  and 
commented on the brilliant discipline of the students in behaviour at Abbey College. As the 
County Councillor Cllr Tobias had been out with the Highways Officer to discuss the state of 
the roads in the community, and the biggest block is the funding to repair underneath the roads 
instead they are only able to fund patching them. Cllr Tobias then went on to discuss the 199 
David Wilson Homes and informed members that further housing would be coming at the RAF 
Upwood   site   and   still   with   no   infrastructure in   place.   Cllr   Tobias   touched   on   the 
Pedestrianisation and welcomed better communication on the project. Cllr Tobias was asked 
by the Mayor if he had any information on the pilot project on resurfacing the Fen Roads – Cllr 
Tobias  had  not.  Cllr  J  Clarke  asked  Cllr  Tobais  about  the  waste  of  resource  on  the  use  of 
traffic  lights  when  no  work  is taking place.  Cllr  Tobias  noted  the  comments.  Cllr  Tobias  did 
state you can read what he had been achieving in his two columns in the local newspaper. 
 
Presentation from Ramsey Neighbourhoods Trust 
Cllr I Axelsen and Cllr J Aubin declared a non-pecuniary interest on this item as Trustees of 
Ramsey Neighbourhoods Trust. 
 
Sam and Sarah from Ramsey Neighbourhoods Trust gave a presentation to members with an 
overview of the community group, what they do and what services they provide. Sarah talked 
through the young people’s projects which Ramsey Town Council funding had been covering. 
Cllr Axelsen who is also the Chair of Ramsey Neighbourhoods Trust had previously circulated 
the funding figures to members. The funding for the following year would be discussed at the 
following Finance Working Party and form part of the 20278/28 budget. 
 
 

2 
 
325. Planning Applications for Consideration: 
 
1.1 3226/01526/FUL Temporary permission for a period of 15 years for the erection of 3 units 
for use as retail or community space and associated public realm and highway 
improvements – Pedestrian Island, Great Whyte, Ramsey. Proposed by Cllr S Corney and 
seconded by Cllr E Welsh Cllr S Corney proposed acceptance of the application. 
Proposed by Cllr A  Austin and seconded by Cllr M Clarke an amendment to Cllr s 
Corney’s proposal ‘There is insufficient information for Ramsey Town Council to be able to 
support the application.’ A vote was taken on the amendment 5 FOR, 3 AGAINST and 6 
ABSTENSIONS. This meant that the amendment became the substantive motion. There 
was confusion for the councillors who voted to abstain as they thought they would then be 
able to vote on the original proposal by Cllr S Corney, this was not the case once the 
amendment had become the substantive motion. The meeting then moved on to planning 
application 1.2  
1.2 25/01301/FUL Erection of owner/site managers dwelling to serve existing caravan site.  
The retention of 14 existing touring caravan pitches, toilet and shower block and 3 holiday 
lodges along with the erection of two new timber holiday lodges and four new holiday 
pods – Riverside Lake and Leisure, Mereside Drove, Ramsey Mereside. Proposed by Cllr 
S Corney and seconded by Cllr P Rose Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for 
the District Council to APPROVE the application. Members were clear their previous 
comments still stood. 
1.3 26/01763/FUL Erection of 3 detached dwellings, 3 detached double garages and 
associated works – Oak Cottage, Forty Foot Bank, Ramsey Forty Foot. Cllrs A Austin, P 
Rose and S Corney declared a non-pecuniary interest as they knew the applicant. 
Proposed by Cllr S Corney and seconded by Cllr J Bufton for District Council to 
APPROVE the application - Ramsey Town Council voted 6 FOR, 8 AGAINST and 1 
ABSTENTION The majority vote was for the application to be REFUSED. Members 
shared the concerns of the neighbouring residents in attendance. 
1.4 26/01763/FUL/26/01764/LBC Proposed conversion and extension of existing curtilage 
listed outbuilding into a separate, independently owned dwellinghouse – Bodsey House, 
Bodsey Toll Road, Ramsey. Proposed by Cllr L Knight and seconded by Cllr P Rose 
Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for the District Council to APPROVE the 
application 
1.5 25/01433/FUL /26/00045/REFUSL Land Far West of Romany Cottage, Bucks Drove, 
Ramsey St Marys. Proposed self-build dwelling to be used as site manager’s house.  
Appeal against refusal. Cllr J Clarke declared a non-pecuniary as a neighbour to the 
applicant. Proposed by Cllr M Clarke and seconded Ramsey Town Council 13 FOR and 2 
ABSTENTIONS for the District Council to keep the REFUSAL in place. Their previous 
comments stood. 
 
326. Planning – other business 
a) Latest Planning Tracker – noted 
b) Planning online training- Members were reminded of the online planning training that 
would take place on zoom on 21
st
 October 2026. The Clerk was asked to circulate the 
invitation again. 
 
327. Finance Items 
a) Financial summary – Cash book to 30/09/2026 – noted 

3 
 
b) Expenditure Transactions to be approved. Proposed by Cllr S Corney and seconded by 
Cllr S Fice Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for the expenditure transactions 
to be APPROVED. 
c) Grant applications – The Clerk informed members that 13 applications had been 
received and they would go to the next Finance Working Party and approved at the 
November Full Council meeting. 
d) Budget 2027/28 – Cllr S Fice informed members that the budget packs would be sent 
out in the following week. 
 
328.Working Party Updates 
 Members to receive an update from the Chairs of each Working Party – the Clerk 
apologised it had not gone out with the agenda papers but circulated that day. 
 
329. Working Party Recommendations 
 Economic Development – Members were informed that the SLA agreement for the 
Discover Huntingdonshire website. 
 Communications – Members were informed that the Newtown Road Play Park 
Consultation had been completed and the response was overwhelmingly positive. 
 
330.Town Mayor’s and Clerk’s Correspondence 
a) Civic Service Feedback – Cllr V Fendley fed back to members on how much people 
appreciated the Civic Service and its community spirit and that a lovely handwritten letter had 
been received by the High Sheriff of Cambridgeshire which would be in the office if any 
member wished to read it. 
b) Zebra Crossing Location, Abbey College Local Highways Initiative Bid – Members were 
informed by Cllr V Fendley that the wording on the consultation had been changed as 
Ramsey Town Council had not supported the zebra crossing due to the loss of parking 
spaces it would cause outside St Thomas a Becket Church. The Clerk was asked to forward 
the link to members. 
c) Local Highways Initiative Bid (Ramsey St Mary’s Buffer zones) update. The Clerk tabled 
the information received from Highways that the bid had not been successful. Further 
clarification had been asked for and it would go to the Amenities, Highways and Leisure 
Working Party. 
d) FOI Feedback – The Clerk informed members that the FOI had been responded to and no 
further communication had taken place. 
e) Newsletter Distribution – The Clerk informed members that the newsletter was being 
distributed and being well received. 
f) Development Management Committee – The Mayor informed members that the DMC 
meeting would take place on the 19
th
 October and members could attend in person, register 
to speak, or watch via zoom. Cllr S Corney would be representing the views at the meeting of 
Ramsey Town Council. 
g) Ramsey Communities Neighbourhood Plan – The Mayor informed members that the 
referendum for the NHP would take place on Thursday 26
th
 November 2026.

metadata.title: Five-bedroom Ellington home on market for offers over £850,000
metadata.contentSnippet: A five-bedroom detached house in Ellington is for sale at offers over £850,000, with open-plan kitchen, south-facing garden, EV charger and nearby schools.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Five-bedroom Ellington home on market for offers over £850,000
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary:
A five-bedroom detached house in Ellington is on the market at offers over £850,000. Selling agent Harvey Robinson said the property offers "a rare blend of contemporary luxury and practical family living". Entering the property, the porch opens to the hallway, which leads to all of the reception rooms, the study and the cloakroom. To the rear of the house is the 33ft open-plan kitchen/dining/family room, with fitted cabinetry, an island, integrated appliances and two sets of glazed doors opening to the garden. The contemporary open-plan kitchen, dining and family room has views of the garden (Image: Mark Holmes Photography) The adjacent utility room has additional storage and a door to outside. There's a more formal dining room to the front of the house. A dual-aspect lounge overlooks the front and rear, with a further set of glazed doors to the garden. The sitting room has glazed doors to the garden (Image: Mark Holmes Photography) Upstairs, the landing leads to all five bedrooms, two with en suites, and a family bathroom. The spacious master bedroom (Image: Mark Holmes Photography) The master bedroom's en-suite bathroom (Image: Mark Holmes Photography) Outside, a brick paved driveway with parking leads to a double garage with an EV charger. The landscaped, south-facing rear garden is mainly laid to lawn with a paved patio and established beds and borders. The south-facing rear garden (Image: Mark Holmes Photography) A hot tub may be available by separate negotiation. The property is situated on Thrapston Road in Ellington, a rural village with scenic walks, cycling routes and bridleways. There are several popular pub/restaurants in the area, including the Mermaid in Ellington. Nearby schools include Spaldwick Primary School and Hinchingbrooke Secondary School. Kimbolton School, an independent day and boarding school, is a short drive away. For more information, contact Harvey Robinson. PROPERTY FACTS

metadata.title: Murder arrest after woman, 61, found dead in Cambridgeshire town
metadata.contentSnippet: A man has been arrested on suspicion of murder after a woman was found dead at a property on Alexandra Road, Wisbech.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Murder arrest after woman, 61, found dead in Cambridgeshire town
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Detectives have made an arrest after a woman was found dead in a Cambridgeshire town. Police were called at around 9.50pm on Saturday (November 21) with reports of a 61-year-old woman found dead at a property in Alexandra Road, Wisbech. A 62-year-old man was arrested at the scene on suspicion of murder and remains in police custody. Police, including specialist scenes of crime officers, remain at the scene and investigations are ongoing, Cambridgeshire Constabulary confirmed. Detective Inspector Andrew Moralee, from the Major Crime Unit, said: "I understand this is likely to be concerning for residents, but we believe this to be an isolated incident and are not looking for anybody else at this time. "Our thoughts are very much with the woman’s family and friends." Anyone with any relevant information is urged to report it online or via 101, quoting Op Emeth. Have you got a story you want to share? Get in touch at oliver.murphy@newsquest.co.uk

metadata.title: Cambridgeshire boy banned from social media after terrorism conviction
metadata.contentSnippet: A boy from Cambridgeshire has been banned from using social media after he was convicted of a terrorism offence.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Cambridgeshire boy banned from social media after terrorism conviction
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A boy from Cambridgeshire has been banned from using social media after he was convicted of a terrorism offence. The 17-year-old was made the subject of a three-year criminal behaviour order preventing him from accessing or using any social networking site. Sentenced at the Old Bailey on November 19, he is also banned from using tools designed to conceal online activity, including VPNs. He will be electronically monitored by tag and curfewed for six months and additionally ordered to fulfil an activity requirement order for 91 days. It follows an investigation into the teenager, who can't be named for legal reasons, by the Eastern Regional Special Operations Unit (ERSOU). The boy, who is now under "intensive supervision" had become an active figure within the so-called Com (short for Community) online network. Members seek status through criminal behaviour, including the encouragement of self-harm, child sexual abuse, violence and the sharing of extremist content. He was initially arrested on April 2 this year. Officers from ERSOU's Counter Terrorism Policing team uncovered evidence of a sustained interest in extreme right-wing ideology. This included references to the proscribed terrorist organisation Maniac Murder Cult (MMC). He was found to have downloaded a prohibited manifesto containing material useful to someone preparing a terrorist attack. The teenager had also created an online group called "Inferno", where members discussed targeting vulnerable individuals and encouraging acts of self-harm. Content recovered from the boy's phone and computer included images depicting apparent injuries. Material linked to people he had encouraged to self-harm was also discovered. He was found to have encouraged young females to create graphic self-harm imagery, to be used in videos and online collages. The offending took place when the boy was aged between 15 and 16. Further enquiries revealed he had accessed indecent images of children, including material showing the most serious category of sexual abuse. He went on to plead guilty at the same court to collecting information likely to be useful to a person committing or preparing an act of terrorism. He also admitted encouraging or assisting serious self harm, making indecent images of children, possession of cannabis and two counts of criminal damage. ERSOU Assistant Chief Officer Hannah Wilkinson said: "This case highlights the growing threat, in particular to children, posed by online communities where extremism, exploitation, self-harm and serious criminality often overlap. "These networks can have a profound and damaging impact on those drawn into them, whether as offenders or victims. "The restrictions, requested by the police and imposed by the court, are significant and are designed to disrupt access to the online environments where this offending developed and reduce the risk of further harm. "They will be rigorously enforced." She added: "Our officers work tirelessly to protect children and vulnerable people from those who involve themselves in Com networks. "Parents and guardians should also be aware that these harmful networks often operate across mainstream online platforms. "Taking an active interest in the online communities young people engage with and having regular conversations with them about what they are accessing, can help identify harmful influences and ensure support is available when needed." Have you got a story you want to share? Get in touch at oliver.murphy@newsquest.co.uk

metadata.title: Diddly Squat Farm Christmas gifts arrive at Huntingdon garden centre
metadata.contentSnippet: A new Diddly Squat Farm Christmas gardening gift range has launched at Huntingdon Garden Centre, featuring seed advent calendars, bulbs and festive grow-your-own presents.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Diddly Squat Farm Christmas gifts arrive at Huntingdon garden centre
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A new Diddly Squat Farm gardening gift collection is on sale at Huntingdon Garden Centre in time for Christmas. Co-produced with Blue Diamond Garden Centres, the range includes a flower-seed advent calendar, spring bulb mixes and a “flaming hot” chilli-growing mug. Lisa Hogan, co-founder of Diddly Squat Farm Shop, said: "We’ve really enjoyed working with Blue Diamond to bring this collection to life. Lisa Hogan with Flaming Hot Mug. (Image: Blue Diamond Garden Centres) "There is something rather satisfying about creating Christmas presents that can actually be grown, planted or used in the garden. "We hope the range brings a bit of fun to Christmas shopping and, of course, a bit of Diddly Squat to gardens across the country." The award-winning Plantable Garden Planner features gardening tips, a logbook and 12 plantable seed papers. The collection also includes Diddly Squat Farm Seedy Balls, a Fruit & Nut Bar and Feeder inspired by Jeremy Clarkson’s love of British birds, a Plantable Notebook, festive Christmas cards and the striking Amaryllis ‘Candy Cane’, christened by Lisa Hogan. Alan Roper, chief executive of Blue Diamond Garden Centres, said: "The countdown to Christmas has begun and there’s a little bit of Diddly Squat Farm arriving with this new co-produced garden gifting collection featuring a range of practical, unique and playful gifts for gardeners, growers and fans of the farm." The collection is available exclusively at Blue Diamond Garden Centres and the Diddly Squat Farm Shop.

metadata.title: Orangutan statue stolen from Cambridgeshire garden centre found two months on
metadata.contentSnippet: An orangutan statue stolen from a garden centre in Horningsea, Cambridgeshire has been found more than two months after it went missing.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Orangutan statue stolen from Cambridgeshire garden centre found two months on
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: An orangutan statue stolen from a garden centre in Cambridgeshire has been found more than two months after it went missing. The figure, valued at £799, was taken from Scotsdales Garden Centre in Horningsea on September 7. Derek Lundgren, 61, of New Road, Sawston, pleaded guilty to the theft and breaching three suspended sentences. Lundgren was sentenced to a year and 11 months in prison (Image: Cambridgeshire Police) He was caught on CCTV leaving the store without paying, before cycling away with the statue across his handlebars. Cambridgeshire Constabulary recovered the orangutan after receiving a tip-off about an address in Teversham. "Sure enough the stolen orangutan was there and a woman was arrested," a post by the force read:. She was given a conditional caution after admitting to receiving stolen goods. Members of the force with the recovered orangutan statue (Image: @cambscops/Instagram) The ape, nicknamed ‘Bruce’ by officers, will now be returned to the garden centre. Lundgren was sentenced to one year and 11 months in prison at Ipswich Magistrates' Court on November 9.

metadata.title: Specialists with main dealer expertise - discover Bartlett Automotive
metadata.contentSnippet: For 17 years, Bartlett Automotive has been providing local vehicle owners with a first-class alternative to the main dealership. Specialising now with BMW, MINI and PORSCHE brands they combine specialist knowledge, exceptional customer service and outstanding value for money. This award-winning family-run Huntingdon business really has earned the trust of thousands of motorists across Cambridgeshire.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Specialists with main dealer expertise - discover Bartlett Automotive
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary:
Brought to you by Bartlett Automotive For 17 years, Bartlett Automotive has been providing local vehicle owners with a first-class alternative to the main dealership. Specialising now with BMW, MINI and PORSCHE brands they combine specialist knowledge, exceptional customer service and outstanding value for money. This award-winning family-run Huntingdon business really has earned the trust of thousands of motorists across Cambridgeshire. When you drive a BMW, MINI or Porsche, you expect exceptional standards of engineering, performance and reliability. So, when it comes to maintaining your vehicle, why should you settle for anything less than expert care? At Bartlett Automotive in Huntingdon, you don't have to. Established in 2009 by husband-and-wife team Damian and Natalie Bartlett, they have spent 17 years building a strong and enviable reputation for specialist vehicle servicing, diagnostics and repairs, offering customers the expertise they would expect from a main dealer, without the premium dealership price tag. Bartlett Automotive has wasted no time growing into one of the area's most trusted independent specialists, welcoming thousands of satisfied customers through its doors. Its reputation speaks for itself. With both local and national awards being achieved, and hundreds of positive Google reviews along with an excellent customer rating, Bartlett Automotive has built its success on something simple: consistently delivering quality workmanship, honest advice and a genuinely personal service. Many customers have trusted Bartlett with their vehicles for years, returning time and again because they know their cars are in capable hands. Behind every successful workshop is a talented team, and Bartlett Automotive is no exception. Its experienced, dealer-trained technicians bring extensive technical knowledge and practical expertise across BMW, MINI and Porsche vehicles. From routine servicing and MOTs to complex diagnostics, engine repairs, timing chains and performance-related maintenance, the team has the equipment and experience to tackle almost anything a main dealership can offer. The Huntingdon workshop is equipped with advanced manufacturer-level diagnostic systems, specialist tooling and technology, allowing technicians to identify faults accurately and carry out repairs to exceptionally high standards. Whether you own a BMW M model, a much-loved MINI Cooper, a Porsche 911 or a family SUV, you can be confident your vehicle is receiving the specialist attention it deserves. One of the biggest misconceptions among motorists is that a vehicle must be serviced by a main dealership to protect its manufacturer warranty - that simply isn't the case. Bartlett Automotive follows manufacturer servicing schedules, uses genuine or approved equivalent-quality components and maintains the appropriate servicing records, helping protect eligible manufacturer warranties. Importantly, the team can also update manufacturer electronic service histories, ensuring servicing is correctly recorded within the relevant online systems, just as customers would expect from their dealership. For owners of newer vehicles, this provides valuable reassurance, maintaining the continuity of their service history while benefiting from substantial savings. metadata.title: Discover stunning National Trust site with 'something for everyone'
metadata.contentSnippet: Love exploring National Trust sites and fancy a nice walk with plenty of activities? Then look no further than this stunning estate.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Discover stunning National Trust site with 'something for everyone'
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Love exploring National Trust sites and fancy a nice walk with plenty of activities? Then look no further than this stunning estate. Described as a "beautiful gem", families can't help but rave about the historic Wimpole Estate, in Arrington, Cambridgeshire. Built on more than 2,000 years of history, it features everything from Iron Age roundhouses to vibrant walled gardens. At the heart of the estate is an impressive 17th-century mansion with intimate family rooms that contrast with "lavish Georgian interiors". Visitors can walk among rare-breed cattle through "grand avenues" before entering shaded woodland. The estate also has a second-hand bookshop filled with gifts, homeware, books, local produce and gardening accessories. There is also a seasonal selection of plants for sale in the courtyard. Meanwhile, the Old Rectory Café offers light lunches, homemade cakes and specials, using produce grown on site. And if this wasn't enough, each year the estate transforms into an illuminated festive trail. More than one million lights form part of dazzling display of festive magic, making it the perfect Christmas evening out. On TripAdvisor, the estate has more than 640 'excellent' reviews, with visitors recommending it as a must visit for families and nature lovers. Elsewhere, on Google Reviews, Wimpole Hall has a score of 4.6 out of 5 from more than 7,800 reviews. It should come as no surprise, then, it has received rave reviews over the years. Unsurprisingly, it has received a tidal wave of rave reviews of the years, with visitors praising it as a "great day out". One recent review read: "Something for all the family. Lots of walks. Historic and working farm with animals up close, lovely gardens and trees. "Places for picnics. The house is well worth taking time over. Volunteers eager to share their knowledge and make sure we didn't miss the most interesting bits. Could even keep children engaged." Another added: "Been going here for years and love it. Great day out. The farms is amazing for kids with an incredible playground. "Beautiful walks round the estate. The house is massive and the guides know their stuff and are always on hand to help out." Have you got a story you want to share? Get in touch at oliver.murphy@newsquest.co.uk

metadata.title: Beloved Cambridgeshire pub seeks new publican after investment
metadata.contentSnippet: The White Horse Pub in Milton, Cambridgeshire is looking for a new operator after recent investment.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Beloved Cambridgeshire pub seeks new publican after investment
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A beloved Cambridgeshire pub is looking for a new operator following recent investment. The White Horse in Milton is seeking a new publican to continue its "excellent reputation" for quality food and hospitality. Stonegate Pub Partners describes it as "a fantastic community pub on Milton High Street that has built a strong reputation for quality food, warm hospitality and its central role in village life". The pool table in The White Horse (Image: Stonegate) The pub has two distinct areas: a restaurant-style dining room with a cosy snug, and a lively sports bar with darts and pool. It also has a large beer garden and customer car park. Katy Jones, regional manager at Stonegate Pub Partners, said: "The White Horse is one of those pubs that sits right at the heart of its community. "It's a much-loved venue with a fantastic reputation for great food and recent investment has ensured it's in excellent condition for its next chapter. "We're looking for an ambitious and passionate publican who can build on the strong foundations already in place while bringing their own ideas and personality to the business." Inside The White Horse (Image: Stonegate) Close to Cambridge, the A14 and Cambridge Science Park, the pub benefits from steady trade all year and easy access. Stonegate Pub Partners wants an experienced publican with a strong hospitality record, business sense and a passion for memorable customer service. The successful applicant will maintain the pub’s strong food and drink offer while strengthening its role as a community hub. Outside The White Horse in Milton (Image: Stonegate) The opportunity also includes spacious three-bedroom accommodation above the pub, suitable for the operator and their family. Candidates interested in the role can find more information on the Stonegate Pub Partners website.
