RAMSEY TOWN COUNCIL 
 
You are hereby summoned to attend a meeting of Ramsey Town Council to be held at 7pm 
on Thursday 22nd October 2026, in The Lavender Room, Ramsey Town Council, Great 
Whyte, Ramsey, when the following items of business will be transacted: - 
 
Please ensure all mobile phones are switched off or turned to silent during the 
meeting. 
The meeting room will open to the public at 18.50. 
 
Lisa Renfree                                      16th October 2026 
   
  
 
  
Town Clerk/RFO 
 
A G E N D A  
 
 
APOLOGIES FOR ABSENCE 
 
1. DECLARATIONS OF INTEREST 
To receive declarations from Members as to disclosable pecuniary and other 
interests and the nature of those interests in relation to any agenda item. 
   
2. PUBLIC PARTICIPATION 
    To allow 20 minutes for any members of the public to address the Council.  
 
3. MINUTES 
To approve as a correct record, the Minutes of the meeting of the Council held on 
8
th
 October 2026 - attached. 
  
4. COUNCILLOR RESIGNATIONS 
Notice is hereby given pursuant to section 87(2) of the Local Government Act 1972 
that due to the resignation of Councillor Ash Austin and Councillor Phil Rose there 
are two vacancies in the Town Council. 
If, within 14 statutory days after the date of this notice, a request for an election to 
fill the vacancy is made in writing to the Returning Officer, Huntingdonshire District 
Council,  Pathfinder  House,  Huntingdon  PE29  3TN  by  ten  electors  of  the town  an 
election will be held.  If no such notice is given the Town Council will fill the vacancy 
by co-option. 
 
5. PLANNING- Members are asked to visit the Huntingdonshire District Council 
Planning Portal to view the plans and documents prior to the meeting. 
 
1.1 26/01809/FUL Erection of a new 2 bed bungalow, 284 Herne Road, Ramsey St 
Mary’s Huntingdon PE26 2TB 
1.2  26/01440/FUL Change of use to a SEN day school (Class F1), erection of a rear 
single storey extension, external alterations to existing two-storey rear extension, 
and associated works including additional car parking, new landscaping, and 
recreation areas, Westward House, Bury Road, Ramsey, Huntingdon PE26 1NA 
1.3 26/01526/FUL Temporary permission for a period of 15 years for the erection of 3 
units for use as retail or community space and associated public realm and 

highway improvements – Pedestrian Island, Great Whyte, Ramsey. This item is on 
the agenda to complete the vote on the substantial motion on 1.1 from the meeting 
of 8
th
 October. The substantive motion is ‘There is insufficient information for 
Ramsey Town Council to be able to support the application.’ If this vote is 
defeated it will return to the original motion ‘To accept the application’ 
 
 Planning – other business 
a) Feedback on Planning online training 21
st
 October. 
b) Feedback on the Development Management Committee reference the David 
Wilson Homes. Cllr S Corney 
c) To agree the representations to be submitted to Huntingdonshire District 
Council in response to their Local Plan consultation (previously circulated) 
 
 
6. MEETING DATES 
The next meeting of Ramsey Town Council will take place on 12th November 2026 at 
7pm.  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 
 
MINUTES OF RAMSEY TOWN COUNCIL MEETING 
held at 7pm on Thursday 08 October 2026 at  
Ramsey Town Council Great Whyte, Ramsey 
 
 
Present:    Councillors: A Austin, I Axelsen, J Bufton, J Clarke, M Clarke, Cllrs S Corney, V 
Fendley (Mayor), S Fice, L Knight, P Rose, R Terrill, J Thompson, L Webster and E Welsh. 
In attendance: Mrs L Renfree, Town Clerk  
 
320. Apologies for Absence. 
 Cllrs A Costello, C Maskell. 
 
321.To Receive Declarations of Interest. 
No declarations of interest were made at that point. 
 
322. Public Participation. 
There  was  six  members  of  the  public  who  discussed  planning  1.3,  discussing  the  potential 
199  David  Wilson  Homes  which  was  going  to  be  debated  on  19
th
 October  at  Development 
Management Panel and a question was raised to be answered post that meeting on where 
the community would stand to make a legal challenge. 
 
323. Minutes of the Last Meeting to be Approved. 
Proposed by Cllr S Corney and seconded by Cllr L Knight, Councillors voted 13 FOR and 2 
ABSTENSIONS for the Minutes of the meeting of the Council held on 24
th
 September 2026 
as a correct record. 
 
324.County and District Councillor Update. 
County and District Councillor Cllr H Tobias attended the meeting to feedback on both County 
and District matters. Cllr Tobias outlined two visits to Ashbeach School and Abbey College 
and  commented  on  the  challenges  that  Ashbeach  faced  with  lack  of  SEN  funding  and 
commented on the brilliant discipline of the students in behaviour at Abbey College. As the 
County Councillor Cllr Tobias had been out with the Highways Officer to discuss the state of 
the roads in the community, and the biggest block is the funding to repair underneath the roads 
instead they are only able to fund patching them. Cllr Tobias then went on to discuss the 199 
David Wilson Homes and informed members that further housing would be coming at the RAF 
Upwood   site   and   still   with   no   infrastructure   in   place.   Cllr   Tobias   touched   on   the 
Pedestrianisation and welcomed better communication on the project. Cllr Tobias was asked 
by the Mayor if he had any information on the pilot project on resurfacing the Fen Roads – Cllr 
Tobias  had  not.  Cllr  J  Clarke  asked  Cllr  Tobais  about  the  waste  of  resource  on  the  use  of 
traffic  lights  when  no  work  is  taking  place.  Cllr  Tobias  noted  the  comments.  Cllr  Tobias did 
state you can read what he had been achieving in his two columns in the local newspaper. 
 
Presentation from Ramsey Neighbourhoods Trust 
Cllr I Axelsen and Cllr J Aubin declared a non-pecuniary interest on this item as Trustees of 
Ramsey Neighbourhoods Trust. 
 
Sam and Sarah from Ramsey Neighbourhoods Trust gave a presentation to members with an 
overview of the community group, what they do and what services they provide. Sarah talked 
through the young people’s projects which Ramsey Town Council funding had been covering. 
Cllr Axelsen who is also the Chair of Ramsey Neighbourhoods Trust had previously circulated 
the funding figures to members. The funding for the following year would be discussed at the 
following Finance Working Party and form part of the 20278/28 budget. 

 
 
325. Planning Applications for Consideration: 
 
1.1 26/01526/FUL Temporary permission for a period of 15 years for the erection of 3 units 
for use as retail or community space and associated public realm and highway 
improvements – Pedestrian Island, Great Whyte, Ramsey. Proposed by Cllr S Corney 
and seconded by Cllr E Welsh Cllr S Corney proposed acceptance of the application. 
Proposed by Cllr A  Austin and seconded by Cllr M Clarke an amendment to Cllr s 
Corney’s proposal ‘There is insufficient information for Ramsey Town Council to be able 
to support the application.’ A vote was taken on the amendment 5 FOR, 3 AGAINST and 
6 ABSTENSIONS. This meant that the amendment became the substantive motion. 
There was confusion for the councillors who voted to abstain as they thought they would 
then be able to vote on the original proposal by Cllr S Corney, this was not the case once 
the amendment had become the substantive motion. The meeting then moved on to 
planning application 1.2  
1.2 25/01301/FUL Erection of owner/site managers dwelling to serve existing caravan site.  
The retention of 14 existing touring caravan pitches, toilet and shower block and 3 holiday 
lodges along with the erection of two new timber holiday lodges and four new holiday 
pods – Riverside Lake and Leisure, Mereside Drove, Ramsey Mereside. Proposed by Cllr 
S Corney and seconded by Cllr P Rose Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for 
the District Council to APPROVE the application. Members were clear their previous 
comments still stood. 
1.3 26/01763/FUL Erection of 3 detached dwellings, 3 detached double garages and 
associated works – Oak Cottage, Forty Foot Bank, Ramsey Forty Foot. Cllrs A Austin, P 
Rose and S Corney declared a non-pecuniary interest as they knew the applicant. 
Proposed by Cllr S Corney and seconded by Cllr J Bufton for District Council to 
APPROVE the application - Ramsey Town Council voted 6 FOR, 8 AGAINST and 1 
ABSTENTION The majority vote was for the application to be REFUSED. Members 
shared the concerns of the neighbouring residents in attendance. 
1.4 26/01763/FUL/26/01764/LBC Proposed conversion and extension of existing curtilage 
listed outbuilding into a separate, independently owned dwellinghouse – Bodsey House, 
Bodsey Toll Road, Ramsey. Proposed by Cllr L Knight and seconded by Cllr P Rose 
Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for the District Council to APPROVE the 
application 
1.5 25/01433/FUL /26/00045/REFUSL Land Far West of Romany Cottage, Bucks Drove, 
Ramsey St Marys. Proposed self-build dwelling to be used as site manager’s house.  
Appeal against refusal. Cllr J Clarke declared a non-pecuniary as a neighbour to the 
applicant. Proposed by Cllr M Clarke and seconded Ramsey Town Council 13 FOR and 2 
ABSTENTIONS for the District Council to keep the REFUSAL in place. Their previous 
comments stood. 
 
326. Planning – other business 
a) Latest Planning Tracker – noted 
b) Planning online training- Members were reminded of the online planning training that 
would take place on zoom on 21
st
 October 2026. The Clerk was asked to circulate the 
invitation again. 
 
327. Finance Items 
a) Financial summary – Cash book to 30/09/2026 – noted 

b) Expenditure Transactions to be approved. Proposed by Cllr S Corney and seconded by 
Cllr S Fice Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for the expenditure transactions 
to be APPROVED. 
c) Grant applications – The Clerk informed members that 13 applications had been 
received and they would go to the next Finance Working Party and approved at the 
November Full Council meeting. 
d) Budget 2027/28 – Cllr S Fice informed members that the budget packs would be sent 
out in the following week. 
 
328.Working Party Updates 
 Members to receive an update from the Chairs of each Working Party – the Clerk 
apologised it had not gone out with the agenda papers but circulated that day. 
 
329. Working Party Recommendations 
 Economic Development – Members were informed that the SLA agreement for the 
Discover Huntingdonshire website. 
 Communications – Members were informed that the Newtown Road Play Park 
Consultation had been completed and the response was overwhelmingly positive. 
 
330.Town Mayor’s and Clerk’s Correspondence 
a) Civic Service Feedback – Cllr V Fendley fed back to members on how much people 
appreciated the Civic Service and its community spirit and that a lovely handwritten letter had 
been received by the High Sheriff of Cambridgeshire which would be in the office if any 
member wished to read it. 
b) Zebra Crossing Location, Abbey College Local Highways Initiative Bid – Members were 
informed by Cllr V Fendley that the wording on the consultation had been changed as 
Ramsey Town Council had not supported the zebra crossing due to the loss of parking 
spaces it would cause outside St Thomas a Becket Church. The Clerk was asked to forward 
the link to members. 
c) Local Highways Initiative Bid (Ramsey St Mary’s Buffer zones) update. The Clerk tabled 
the information received from Highways that the bid had not been successful. Further 
clarification had been asked for and it would go to the Amenities, Highways and Leisure 
Working Party. 
d) FOI Feedback – The Clerk informed members that the FOI had been responded to and no 
further communication had taken place. 
e) Newsletter Distribution – The Clerk informed members that the newsletter was being 
distributed and being well received. 
f) Development Management Committee – The Mayor informed members that the DMC 
meeting would take place on the 19
th
 October and members could attend in person, register 
to speak, or watch via zoom. Cllr S Corney would be representing the views at the meeting of 
Ramsey Town Council. 
g) Ramsey Communities Neighbourhood Plan – The Mayor informed members that the 
referendum for the NHP would take place on Thursday 26
th
 November 2026. 
 
331. Car Park Land Lease 
To discuss the Heads of Terms for the lease – the Clerk had previously circulated the Heads 
of Terms for comment. Cllr J Clarke asked if the Clerk could push for a longer lease than 50 
years. No other comments were asked to be sent back to HDC. Once the lease has gone 
through HDC Legal it will come to members for sign off. 
 
332. Attendances at Meetings and Organisations 
a) Flood Action Planning Meeting – Cllr J Thompson fed back to members about the meeting 
and that the flood action group should be community led, focussed, and tested. 

b) Emergency Planning for the Future – Cllr V Fendley informed members that the meeting 
had 16 residents in attendance a very robust discussion had taken place. Cllr J Thompson 
had taken on the responsibility of outing the actions into the provided template. 
c) LVEP Conference – Cllr V Fendley explained the LVEP positioning starting at the bottom 
with Discover Ramsey, then Discover Huntingdonshire, Loval Visitor Economy Partnership 
and topped by Visit England. Cllr L Knight fed back to members about the Local Visitor 
Economy Forum Conference. It was a very positive meeting with a shout out to Ramsey for 
signing the Service Level Agreement for Discover Huntingdonshire. Both Cllr L K night and 
Cllr V Fendley both attended and sat on the table with Visit England. 
 
333. Meeting Dates 
The next meeting of Ramsey Town Council would take place on Thursday 22nd October 
(Planning) at 7pm.

paragraphs: RAMSEY TOWN COUNCIL

You are hereby summoned to attend a meeting of Ramsey Town Council to be held at 7pm on Thursday 22nd October 2026, in The Lavender Room, Ramsey Town Council, Great Whyte, Ramsey, when the following items of business will be transacted: -
Please ensure all mobile phones are switched off or turned to silent during the meeting. The meeting room will open to the public at 18.50.
Lisa Renfree                                      16th October 2026
Town Clerk/RFO
A G E N D A
APOLOGIES FOR ABSENCE
1. DECLARATIONS OF INTEREST To receive declarations from Members as to disclosable pecuniary and other interests and the nature of those interests in relation to any agenda item.
2. PUBLIC PARTICIPATION To allow 20 minutes for any members of the public to address the Council.
3. MINUTES To approve as a correct record, the Minutes of the meeting of the Council held on 8 th October 2026 - attached.

4. COUNCILLOR RESIGNATIONS Notice is hereby given pursuant to section 87(2) of the Local Government Act 1972 that due to the resignation of Councillor Ash Austin and Councillor Phil Rose there are two vacancies in the Town Council. If, within 14 statutory days after the date of this notice, a request for an election to fill the vacancy is made in writing to the Returning Officer, Huntingdonshire District Council,  Pathfinder  House,  Huntingdon  PE29  3TN  by  ten  electors  of  the town  an election will be held.  If no such notice is given the Town Council will fill the vacancy by co-option.
5. PLANNING- Members are asked to visit the Huntingdonshire District Council Planning Portal to view the plans and documents prior to the meeting.

1.1 26/01809/FUL Erection of a new 2 bed bungalow, 284 Herne Road, Ramsey St Mary’s Huntingdon PE26 2TB 1.2  26/01440/FUL Change of use to a SEN day school (Class F1), erection of a rear single storey extension, external alterations to existing two-storey rear extension, and associated works including additional car parking, new landscaping, and recreation areas, Westward House, Bury Road, Ramsey, Huntingdon PE26 1NA 1.3 26/01526/FUL Temporary permission for a period of 15 years for the erection of 3 units for use as retail or community space and associated public realm and

highway improvements – Pedestrian Island, Great Whyte, Ramsey. This item is on the agenda to complete the vote on the substantial motion on 1.1 from the meeting of 8 th October. The substantive motion is ‘There is insufficient information for Ramsey Town Council to be able to support the application.’ If this vote is defeated it will return to the original motion ‘To accept the application’

Planning – other business a) Feedback on Planning online training 21 st October. b) Feedback on the Development Management Committee reference the David Wilson Homes. Cllr S Corney c) To agree the representations to be submitted to Huntingdonshire District Council in response to their Local Plan consultation (previously circulated)
6. MEETING DATES The next meeting of Ramsey Town Council will take place on 12th November 2026 at 7pm.
MINUTES OF RAMSEY TOWN COUNCIL MEETING held at 7pm on Thursday 08 October 2026 at Ramsey Town Council Great Whyte, Ramsey

Present:    Councillors: A Austin, I Axelsen, J Bufton, J Clarke, M Clarke, Cllrs S Corney, V Fendley (Mayor), S Fice, L Knight, P Rose, R Terrill, J Thompson, L Webster and E Welsh. In attendance: Mrs L Renfree, Town Clerk
320. Apologies for Absence. Cllrs A Costello, C Maskell.
321.To Receive Declarations of Interest. No declarations of interest were made at that point.

322. Public Participation. There  was  six  members  of  the  public  who  discussed  planning  1.3,  discussing  the  potential 199  David  Wilson  Homes  which  was  going  to  be  debated  on  19 th October  at  Development Management Panel and a question was raised to be answered post that meeting on where the community would stand to make a legal challenge.

323. Minutes of the Last Meeting to be Approved. Proposed by Cllr S Corney and seconded by Cllr L Knight, Councillors voted 13 FOR and 2 ABSTENSIONS for the Minutes of the meeting of the Council held on 24 th September 2026 as a correct record.

324.County and District Councillor Update. County and District Councillor Cllr H Tobias attended the meeting to feedback on both County and District matters. Cllr Tobias outlined two visits to Ashbeach School and Abbey College and  commented  on  the  challenges  that  Ashbeach  faced  with  lack  of  SEN  funding  and commented on the brilliant discipline of the students in behaviour at Abbey College. As the County Councillor Cllr Tobias had been out with the Highways Officer to discuss the state of the roads in the community, and the biggest block is the funding to repair underneath the roads instead they are only able to fund patching them. Cllr Tobias then went on to discuss the 199 David Wilson Homes and informed members that further housing would be coming at the RAF Upwood   site   and   still   with   no   infrastructure   in   place.   Cllr   Tobias   touched   on   the Pedestrianisation and welcomed better communication on the project. Cllr Tobias was asked by the Mayor if he had any information on the pilot project on resurfacing the Fen Roads – Cllr Tobias  had  not.  Cllr  J  Clarke  asked  Cllr  Tobais  about  the  waste  of  resource  on  the  use  of traffic  lights  when  no  work  is  taking  place.  Cllr  Tobias  noted  the  comments.  Cllr  Tobias did state you can read what he had been achieving in his two columns in the local newspaper.
Presentation from Ramsey Neighbourhoods Trust Cllr I Axelsen and Cllr J Aubin declared a non-pecuniary interest on this item as Trustees of Ramsey Neighbourhoods Trust.

Sam and Sarah from Ramsey Neighbourhoods Trust gave a presentation to members with an overview of the community group, what they do and what services they provide. Sarah talked through the young people’s projects which Ramsey Town Council funding had been covering. Cllr Axelsen who is also the Chair of Ramsey Neighbourhoods Trust had previously circulated the funding figures to members. The funding for the following year would be discussed at the following Finance Working Party and form part of the 20278/28 budget.
325. Planning Applications for Consideration:

1.1 26/01526/FUL Temporary permission for a period of 15 years for the erection of 3 units for use as retail or community space and associated public realm and highway improvements – Pedestrian Island, Great Whyte, Ramsey. Proposed by Cllr S Corney and seconded by Cllr E Welsh Cllr S Corney proposed acceptance of the application. Proposed by Cllr A  Austin and seconded by Cllr M Clarke an amendment to Cllr s Corney’s proposal ‘There is insufficient information for Ramsey Town Council to be able to support the application.’ A vote was taken on the amendment 5 FOR, 3 AGAINST and 6 ABSTENSIONS. This meant that the amendment became the substantive motion. There was confusion for the councillors who voted to abstain as they thought they would then be able to vote on the original proposal by Cllr S Corney, this was not the case once the amendment had become the substantive motion. The meeting then moved on to planning application 1.2 1.2 25/01301/FUL Erection of owner/site managers dwelling to serve existing caravan site. The retention of 14 existing touring caravan pitches, toilet and shower block and 3 holiday lodges along with the erection of two new timber holiday lodges and four new holiday pods – Riverside Lake and Leisure, Mereside Drove, Ramsey Mereside. Proposed by Cllr S Corney and seconded by Cllr P Rose Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for the District Council to APPROVE the application. Members were clear their previous comments still stood. 1.3 26/01763/FUL Erection of 3 detached dwellings, 3 detached double garages and associated works – Oak Cottage, Forty Foot Bank, Ramsey Forty Foot. Cllrs A Austin, P Rose and S Corney declared a non-pecuniary interest as they knew the applicant. Proposed by Cllr S Corney and seconded by Cllr J Bufton for District Council to APPROVE the application - Ramsey Town Council voted 6 FOR, 8 AGAINST and 1 ABSTENTION The majority vote was for the application to be REFUSED. Members shared the concerns of the neighbouring residents in attendance. 1.4 26/01763/FUL/26/01764/LBC Proposed conversion and extension of existing curtilage listed outbuilding into a separate, independently owned dwellinghouse – Bodsey House, Bodsey Toll Road, Ramsey. Proposed by Cllr L Knight and seconded by Cllr P Rose Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for the District Council to APPROVE the application 1.5 25/01433/FUL /26/00045/REFUSL Land Far West of Romany Cottage, Bucks Drove, Ramsey St Marys. Proposed self-build dwelling to be used as site manager’s house. Appeal against refusal. Cllr J Clarke declared a non-pecuniary as a neighbour to the applicant. Proposed by Cllr M Clarke and seconded Ramsey Town Council 13 FOR and 2 ABSTENTIONS for the District Council to keep the REFUSAL in place. Their previous comments stood.

326. Planning – other business a) Latest Planning Tracker – noted b) Planning online training- Members were reminded of the online planning training that would take place on zoom on 21 st October 2026. The Clerk was asked to circulate the invitation again.
327. Finance Items a) Financial summary – Cash book to 30/09/2026 – noted

b) Expenditure Transactions to be approved. Proposed by Cllr S Corney and seconded by Cllr S Fice Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for the expenditure transactions to be APPROVED. c) Grant applications – The Clerk informed members that 13 applications had been received and they would go to the next Finance Working Party and approved at the November Full Council meeting. d) Budget 2027/28 – Cllr S Fice informed members that the budget packs would be sent out in the following week.
328.Working Party Updates Members to receive an update from the Chairs of each Working Party – the Clerk apologised it had not gone out with the agenda papers but circulated that day.

329. Working Party Recommendations Economic Development – Members were informed that the SLA agreement for the Discover Huntingdonshire website. Communications – Members were informed that the Newtown Road Play Park Consultation had been completed and the response was overwhelmingly positive.

330.Town Mayor’s and Clerk’s Correspondence a) Civic Service Feedback – Cllr V Fendley fed back to members on how much people appreciated the Civic Service and its community spirit and that a lovely handwritten letter had been received by the High Sheriff of Cambridgeshire which would be in the office if any member wished to read it. b) Zebra Crossing Location, Abbey College Local Highways Initiative Bid – Members were informed by Cllr V Fendley that the wording on the consultation had been changed as Ramsey Town Council had not supported the zebra crossing due to the loss of parking spaces it would cause outside St Thomas a Becket Church. The Clerk was asked to forward the link to members. c) Local Highways Initiative Bid (Ramsey St Mary’s Buffer zones) update. The Clerk tabled the information received from Highways that the bid had not been successful. Further clarification had been asked for and it would go to the Amenities, Highways and Leisure Working Party. d) FOI Feedback – The Clerk informed members that the FOI had been responded to and no further communication had taken place. e) Newsletter Distribution – The Clerk informed members that the newsletter was being distributed and being well received. f) Development Management Committee – The Mayor informed members that the DMC meeting would take place on the 19 th October and members could attend in person, register to speak, or watch via zoom. Cllr S Corney would be representing the views at the meeting of Ramsey Town Council. g) Ramsey Communities Neighbourhood Plan – The Mayor informed members that the referendum for the NHP would take place on Thursday 26 th November 2026.

331. Car Park Land Lease To discuss the Heads of Terms for the lease – the Clerk had previously circulated the Heads of Terms for comment. Cllr J Clarke asked if the Clerk could push for a longer lease than 50 years. No other comments were asked to be sent back to HDC. Once the lease has gone through HDC Legal it will come to members for sign off.

332. Attendances at Meetings and Organisations a) Flood Action Planning Meeting – Cllr J Thompson fed back to members about the meeting and that the flood action group should be community led, focussed, and tested.

b) Emergency Planning for the Future – Cllr V Fendley informed members that the meeting had 16 residents in attendance a very robust discussion had taken place. Cllr J Thompson had taken on the responsibility of outing the actions into the provided template. c) LVEP Conference – Cllr V Fendley explained the LVEP positioning starting at the bottom with Discover Ramsey, then Discover Huntingdonshire, Loval Visitor Economy Partnership and topped by Visit England. Cllr L Knight fed back to members about the Local Visitor Economy Forum Conference. It was a very positive meeting with a shout out to Ramsey for signing the Service Level Agreement for Discover Huntingdonshire. Both Cllr L K night and Cllr V Fendley both attended and sat on the table with Visit England.
333. Meeting Dates The next meeting of Ramsey Town Council would take place on Thursday 22nd October (Planning) at 7pm.
